Introduction

Material web, also known as Material Web Components or MWC, is a library of web components that follows Google's Material Design guidelines.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/intro/

What is Material?

Link to “What is Material?” #

Material Design is a design system built and supported by Google designers and developers. Guidelines for building Material apps and components are published on material.io.

Version 3.0 implements Material 3 Expressive, the latest evolution of Material 3: a larger shape scale with shape morphing, spring-based motion, an emphasized type scale, and an updated dynamic color system. The elements are named md-gb-*, follow the WAI-ARIA patterns for their roles, and only rely on web platform features that are Baseline widely available (newer features are guarded and degrade gracefully).

What are web components?

Link to “What are web components?” #

Web components are custom HTML elements with encapsulated styles and behavior. They work across many different frameworks (such as Lit, React, Vue, and Svelte) as well as web environments (such as Eleventy, Wordpress, and Ruby on Rails).

Many components in this library are drop-in replacements for browser elements like <button> and <input>. Every element is prefixed with md-gb-.

What are tokens?

Link to “What are tokens?” #

Design tokens are the building blocks of all UI elements. Here they are CSS custom properties that you can override to style components. Version 3.0 provides the system tokens for color, typography, shape, elevation, space, and motion.

Spec compliance

What the spec checks, ARIA and axe results, Baseline use and size budgets say about md-gb-* components.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/compliance/

How compliance is measured

Link to “How compliance is measured” #

The numbers on this page come from the repository itself and are regenerated by node scripts/m3/gen-compliance-page.mjs (--check fails when this page is stale). The M3 spec is downloaded with npm run m3:update, split into units (a sentence, list item, table row or image description, each with an id), and node scripts/m3/spec-checks.mjs --offline records what happens to each one in .m3-specs/spec-checks/units.json. Only unit counts and ids are used here, never spec text.

Spec units

Link to “Spec units” #

A unit is buildable when the classifier scores it at 0.3 or more (it describes something a component can do, not a caption or designer advice). Tested units are cited from a *_test.ts file under labs/gb or scripts/m3 (spec: <unit id>). Excluded units have a written reason in scripts/m3/exclusions/*.md (spec-exclude:). Tracked units are known gaps listed in scripts/m3/CHECKLIST.md (spec-gap:). Uncovered units are buildable, with no status and no test; the target is 0.

Token audit

Link to “Token audit” #

node scripts/m3/audit-gb.mjs --gaps compares every token declaration in the labs/gb token files with the M3 token database. Match means the value equals the spec; derived means it is computed from a matching token; drift differs from the spec; no spec token has no counterpart in the database; gaps are tokens the Compose reference uses that no gb declaration implements.

Overall: 2415 declarations, 1949 match, 23 derived, 10 drift (0 high-confidence), 433 with no spec token, 10 spec tokens not implemented.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #

Two central suites render rows in labs/gb/components/shared/central and run in a real browser:

  • axe (axe_test.ts): axe-core with no rule disabled, on every subject of the central table (subjects.ts) plus 29 overlay rows in their open state (axe-helpers.ts).
  • ARIA 1.3 (aria_test.ts): the axe rows plus 34 rows that put components in the states ARIA depends on (selected, checked, expanded, grouped, with panels, with an error), checked against the WAI-ARIA 1.3 role and attribute rules. 27 rows are open overlays, so the checks that flip state skip them.

Known gaps are rows with a real violation. They move to axe_gap.ts and aria_gap.ts (red on purpose) and are recorded in AXE_GAPS and ARIA_GAPS. Today: axe none; ARIA none. Suite files: aria_gap.ts, aria_test.ts, axe_gap.ts, axe_test.ts.

Baseline

Link to “Baseline” #

npm run gb:baseline maps every CSS feature in the compiled labs/gb CSS to its web-features Baseline status. A feature that is not widely available must sit inside a matching @supports guard or be listed with a reason in scripts/gb-baseline-allow.json; anything else fails the run.

  • CSS: 19,541 feature uses in 62 files; 51 features are not widely available, used 754 times (478 guarded, 276 allowed with a reason, 0 unguarded). Result: passes.
  • JavaScript (report only): 31 tracked Web API members in 207 source files; 6 are not widely available, 3 of them with at least one use that is not feature-detected.

Quick Start

For fast prototyping, use a CDN such as esm.run to load @material/web without installing it.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/quick-start/

CDN

Link to “CDN” #

For fast prototyping, use a CDN such as esm.run to load @material/web without installing it. The M3 Expressive elements are under @material/web/labs/gb/.

One line

Link to “One line” #

The quickest start is one script. labs/gb/all.js defines every md-gb-* element and adopts the M3 styles into the page. It loads every component, so use it for prototypes only. The import map is optional here; it lets you also import single files by path later. The script tags have no visible effect, so they are a plain block (Download & copy in the page tools menu copies them):

<script type="importmap">
  {"imports": {"@material/web/": "https://esm.run/@material/web/"}}
</script>
<script type="module" src="https://esm.run/@material/web/labs/gb/all.js"></script>

The same module, imported from a script, with a button that needs no other setup:

Only what you use

Link to “Only what you use” #

To load only the elements a page uses, import each one. The import map resolves the bare specifiers (it is the only part of this setup that has no visible effect, so it is a plain block):

<script type="importmap">
  {"imports": {"@material/web/": "https://esm.run/@material/web/"}}
</script>

For production, follow the install and build steps below.

Install

Link to “Install” #

Install Material web components using npm and node.

npm install @material/web

Import

Link to “Import” #

Import each element from @material/web/labs/gb/components/<component>/md-gb-<component>.js, and load the design tokens once with adoptStyles().

Usage

Link to “Usage” #

Use the <md-gb-component> tag in HTML markup. Each component page, such as Button, has more guidance.

Building

Link to “Building” #

Bare module specifiers such as @material/web/... need a tool to resolve them until import maps are adopted. For a more in-depth guide, follow lit.dev's modern build for production.

Rollup quick start

Link to “Rollup quick start” #

Rollup with a plugin that resolves bare module specifiers bundles the entrypoint into one file.

npm install rollup @rollup/plugin-node-resolve
npx rollup -p @rollup/plugin-node-resolve index.js -o bundle.js
 
<script src="./bundle.js"></script>

Migration

Version 3.0 renames most elements from md- to md-gb- and moves them to Material 3 Expressive.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/migration/

Version 3.0 renames most elements from md-* to md-gb-* and moves them to Material 3 Expressive. Many names stay the same, but some attributes and slots change, and a few components are no longer recommended. This page lists the changes. The 2.5.0 docs stay on the root of this site.

Start with the styles

Link to “Start with the styles” #

Load the 3.0 design tokens once per document:

Then import each md-gb-* element you use from @material/web/labs/gb/components/.

Element and attribute map

Link to “Element and attribute map” #

Element names change as listed below. Where the table says "dropped", the 2.5.0 attribute has no 3.0 counterpart and you can remove it.

2.5.0 3.0 Changes
md-filled-button md-gb-button color="filled"
md-elevated-button md-gb-button color="elevated"
md-filled-tonal-button md-gb-button color="tonal"
md-outlined-button md-gb-button color="outlined"
md-text-button md-gb-button color="text"
md-icon-button md-gb-icon-button color="standard"; toggle and flip-icon-in-rtl dropped
md-filled-icon-button md-gb-icon-button color="filled"
md-filled-tonal-icon-button md-gb-icon-button color="tonal"
md-outlined-icon-button md-gb-icon-button color="outlined"
md-fab, md-branded-fab md-gb-fab variant becomes color (primary-container, secondary-container, tertiary-container); size="large" becomes size="lg"; label becomes text content; size, lowered and variant dropped
md-checkbox md-gb-checkbox touch-target dropped
md-radio md-gb-radio touch-target dropped
md-switch md-gb-switch none
md-slider md-gb-slider aria-* label and value text attributes renamed (see below)
md-divider md-gb-divider inset, inset-start and inset-end dropped
md-list, md-list-item md-gb-list, md-gb-list-item start slot becomes leading, end becomes trailing, trailing-supporting-text becomes trailing-text; headline slot is unwrapped
md-menu, md-menu-item md-gb-menu, md-gb-menu-item positioning, menu-corner and anchor-corner dropped on md-gb-menu; the same slot changes as lists
md-linear-progress md-gb-progress indeterminate, buffer and four-color dropped
md-circular-progress md-gb-progress circular indeterminate and four-color dropped
md-filled-text-field md-gb-text-field none (filled is the default)
md-outlined-text-field md-gb-text-field variant="outlined"
md-filled-select md-gb-select menu-positioning, clamp-menu-width, menu-align and quick dropped
md-outlined-select md-gb-select variant="outlined", same drops as above
md-select-option md-gb-select-option headline slot is unwrapped; start becomes leading, end becomes trailing
md-dialog md-gb-dialog the content slot is removed, so the content goes in the default slot
md-tabs md-gb-tabs variant="secondary" when it holds secondary tabs; auto-activate and active-tab-index dropped
md-primary-tab, md-secondary-tab md-gb-tab the label goes in slot="label"; inline-icon, has-icon, active and icon-only dropped
md-chip-set md-gb-chip-set none
md-assist-chip md-gb-chip color="elevated" if it was elevated; label becomes text content
md-filter-chip md-gb-chip type="filter"; same color rule
md-input-chip md-gb-chip type="input" with removable
md-suggestion-chip md-gb-chip type="suggestion"; same color rule
md-icon md-gb-icon inside a button, icon button, FAB or tab, the slot="icon" is removed and the icon goes in DOM order

If the icon is not an md-icon (for example an inline SVG), wrap it in md-gb-icon.

Attributes to rename by hand

Link to “Attributes to rename by hand” #

Converting the elements does not rename every attribute. Update these by hand:

  • md-gb-slider: aria-label-start becomes label-start, aria-label-end becomes label-end, aria-valuetext-start becomes valuetext-start, and aria-valuetext-end becomes valuetext-end. The aria- prefix is reserved for ARIA attributes, so the 3.0 names do not use it. value-label-start and value-label-end keep their names.
  • md-gb-dialog: full-screen applies only on compact windows. Above that, the dialog is a basic dialog with the same slots. Add always-full-screen to keep the full-screen layout at every window size. The 2.5.0 md-dialog has no full-screen attribute, so this is new in 3.0.

Recommendations that changed

Link to “Recommendations that changed” #

The Expressive spec no longer recommends some 2.5.0 patterns. The components remain available, but for new work use the replacement below.

  • Segmented buttons are replaced by a connected button group: md-gb-button-group variant="connected".
  • Navigation drawer is replaced by an expanded navigation rail: md-gb-nav-rail with expanded. Use modal when it overlays content.
  • Bottom app bar is replaced by a docked toolbar: md-gb-toolbar docked.
  • Medium and large app bars are replaced by medium and large flexible app bars: md-gb-app-bar size="md" and size="lg".
  • Small FABs and surface-colored FABs are replaced by the default FAB size and the container colors (primary-container, secondary-container, tertiary-container).

Watch out for

Link to “Watch out for” #
  • Chips and FABs no longer take their text from a label attribute. Put the text in the element instead, as the table shows.
  • An md-gb-* element that is not imported is not upgraded, so it renders as an unknown element.
  • Selectors, queries and tests that use the old md-* tag names need the new names too.

Roadmap

This roadmap describes current, future, and past goals for Material Web Components.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/roadmap/

Current

Link to “Current” #

Version 3.0 (labs/gb) is the M3 Expressive implementation of MWC. It adds Expressive components (such as the button group, split button, FAB menu, carousel, loading indicator, and toolbar), dynamic color, the Expressive shape, type, and motion systems, WAI-ARIA 1.3 conformance, and Web Platform Baseline fallbacks. Version 2.5.0 remains in maintenance mode.

Future

Link to “Future” #

Note: No future work is planned while MWC is in maintenance mode. These roadmap items represent what used to be planned.

New components

Link to “New components” #

Version 3.0 builds every component in the list 2.5.0 planned except these:

  • Autocomplete
  • Banner
  • Data table

The badge, bottom sheet, card, date and time pickers, navigation bar, drawer and rail, search, segmented button, snackbar, tooltip and top app bar are in labs/gb. The toolbar replaces the bottom app bar in M3 Expressive.

Expand Material Design tokens

Link to “Expand Material Design tokens” #

Version 3.0 has the shape and motion system tokens.

We also want to make it easier to use Material Design tokens, such as applying Material typescale, shape, and color to your own components.

Density and spacing tokens

Link to “Density and spacing tokens” #

Density allows components to take up less vertical space for larger displays. While we have some spacing tokens already, we need a comprehensive spacing system to fully support density across components.

Create TSX components

Link to “Create TSX components” #

TSX is a popular language extension for frameworks like React. We want to make it easier and more seamless to use Material Web Components in TSX.

Explore Material Design layouts

Link to “Explore Material Design layouts” #

Components are only part of the story to build fully expressive Material Design applications. We want to explore ways to support building applications that follow Material's layout patterns.

Past

Link to “Past” #

Follow accessibility best practices

Link to “Follow accessibility best practices” #

Completed in Q1 2024

Everyone should be able to access and enjoy the web. We want our components to help others build accessible experiences. The following screen readers are fully supported:

  • VoiceOver
  • Talkback
  • ChromeVox
  • JAWS
  • NVDA

Support

Version 3.0 targets Baseline widely available: the web platform features it uses have worked in all major browsers for at least 30 months.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/support/

Browsers

Link to “Browsers” #

Version 3.0 targets Baseline widely available: the web platform features it uses have worked in all major browsers for at least 30 months. Newer features (such as corner-shape or light-dark()) are only used behind @supports guards or with a fallback, so components stay usable in older engines. The repository checks this with npm run gb:baseline. See Browser support for the minimum versions.

FAQ

Link to “FAQ” #

How do I change the color of a button?

Link to “How do I change the color of a button?” #

Components read --md-sys-color-* tokens. Override the key color a component uses on the element or a class. Buttons use primary, and the states (hover, focus, pressed) are derived from it.

Why doesn't prefers-color-scheme: dark switch the theme?

Link to “Why doesn't prefers-color-scheme: dark switch the theme?” #

The tokens use light-dark(), so they follow the color-scheme property. Set it to follow the system, or force a scheme on any subtree.

How do I generate my own --md-sys-color-* tokens?

Link to “How do I generate my own --md-sys-color-* tokens?” #

Generate a theme from a source color at runtime, or export a stylesheet.

You can also design a scheme with the Material Theme Builder Figma plugin. See Color.

How do I style an element inside another component?

Link to “How do I style an element inside another component?” #

Use CSS ::part(). The parts of each component are listed under its CSS parts in the API reference.

Bundle Sizes

Every md-gb- component is checked against a Brotli-compressed size budget for its JavaScript and CSS (the measured size plus 10% headroom), defined in scripts/size/gb-budgets.json.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/size/

Every md-gb-* component is checked against a Brotli-compressed size budget for its JavaScript and CSS (the measured size plus 10% headroom), defined in scripts/size/gb-budgets.json. For example, md-gb-button stays within about 4.8 KB of JavaScript and 1.5 KB of CSS, and md-gb-badge within about 1 KB and 0.5 KB. Import only the components you use to keep your bundle small.

Browser support

Version 3.0 only uses web platform features that are Baseline widely available.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/browser-support/

Targets

Link to “Targets” #

Version 3.0 only uses web platform features that are Baseline widely available. The oldest browsers the build checks against are:

Browser Minimum version
Chrome 124
Edge 124
Firefox 125
Safari 17.4
iOS Safari 17.4

node scripts/gb-css-validate.mjs prints these values, and the CSS is compiled against them. They move as Baseline moves, so rerun the script to see the current numbers.

Features behind a fallback

Link to “Features behind a fallback” #

Newer features are either guarded with @supports or allowed to be ignored where a browser lacks them. The exceptions are listed, with the reason for each, in scripts/gb-baseline-allow.json. In short:

  • field-sizing: a textarea keeps its fixed rows and scrolls.
  • interpolate-size: size changes to intrinsic keywords jump instead of animating.
  • starting-style: an element appears without its enter transition.
  • transition-behavior: discrete properties change at once.
  • scrollbar-gutter: no reserved gutter, so a small layout shift when a scrollbar appears.
  • overscroll-behavior: scroll chaining at the edge is not contained.
  • view-transitions: the view transition styles never match.
  • container-scroll-state-queries: the app bar does not switch to its stuck look.
  • forced-colors: ignored where forced colors mode does not exist (Safari).

Guard your own newer CSS the same way, so older browsers keep a usable fallback:

Check your own app

Link to “Check your own app” #

Test on the oldest version of each browser in the table, not only the current release. To see which Baseline features the repository uses, run npm run gb:baseline.

AI agents

labs/gb/skill/ is a Claude Code skill named md-gb.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/ai-agents/

What the skill is

Link to “What the skill is” #

labs/gb/skill/ is a Claude Code skill named md-gb. It teaches an agent which md-gb-* element to pick, and each element's attributes, properties, slots, events, CSS parts, custom properties, and what the app must provide itself. It is one SKILL.md plus a reference file per component.

Install it

Link to “Install it” #

Copy the folder into your skills directory. For all of your projects:

mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/md-gb
cp -r labs/gb/skill/. ~/.claude/skills/md-gb/

To share it with one repository, copy it to .claude/skills/md-gb/ in that repository instead. Claude Code loads it when you write HTML, Lit templates, or CSS that use md-gb-* elements.

Install it from this site

Link to “Install it from this site” #

Without a checkout, the skill files are published at /3.0/skill/. The page tools button (bottom end of every page) opens Download & copy, which has Copy agent prompt: paste it into your agent and it creates the skills folder, downloads SKILL.md and every reference/*.md file listed in /3.0/skill/index.json, installs @material/web, and checks the result.

The same menu downloads the whole API as one custom-elements.json (a Custom Elements Manifest of every element), and /3.0/llms.txt indexes the docs as Markdown.

Keep it current

Link to “Keep it current” #

The skill is generated from the component sources and scripts/m3/CHECKLIST.md. Do not edit it by hand. To regenerate it, run:

node scripts/m3/gen-agent-skill.mjs

Run the same command with --check to fail when the output is stale. After you change a component, regenerate the skill and copy it again, because an installed copy does not update itself.

Browser agents (WebMCP)

Link to “Browser agents (WebMCP)” #

On every page of these docs, a browser that supports WebMCP lets its agent search and read the docs through five read-only tools. Nothing is registered in other browsers. The tools use the same search as the Cmd+K dialog, and every page is also available as Markdown at its URL plus .md.

  • search_docs finds sections by keywords: {query, limit?}.
  • get_page returns a page or one section as Markdown: {path, section?}.
  • list_pages lists the pages, optionally of one section: {section?}.
  • get_component_api returns the properties, slots, events, methods, CSS parts and custom properties of an element: {tag}.
  • get_current_page describes the page the user is on, with its outline.

An agent calls them through the browser. This demo calls the same functions the page registers (window.gbDocsTools) and shows the first three results of a search.

Watch out

Link to “Watch out” #
  • The skill covers the md-gb-* elements of 3.0 only. For 2.5.0 md-* elements, use the v2.5.0 documentation.
  • Each reference file lists what the app must provide itself. Check those lines before you rely on the agent's markup.

Debugging

The shared plumbing of the components (motion waits, overflow measure passes, and scroll steps) can record performance marks.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/debugging/

Performance track

Link to “Performance track” #

The shared plumbing of the components (motion waits, overflow measure passes, and scroll steps) can record performance marks. They show up in the Chrome DevTools Performance panel as a custom track named md-gb, in the group Material. The marks are off by default.

Turn them on

Link to “Turn them on” #

The flag is read once, on first use, so set it before you interact with the components. Use any one of these:

  • Add ?md-gb-perf to the page address and load it.
  • Set the flag in the console, then reload. Any value turns the marks on, even 0. Remove the key to turn them off (the first sample below).
  • Set globalThis.MD_GB_DEBUG_PERF = true before any component runs (the second sample below).

Record a trace

Link to “Record a trace” #

Open the Performance panel, start a recording, use the component, and stop it. Look for the md-gb track. Each span is also a performance.measure() entry:

When the flag is off, each call costs one boolean check and allocates nothing.

Use with shadcn/ui

Install the md-gb elements as React components with the shadcn CLI, themed by your shadcn variables.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/shadcn/

What you get

Link to “What you get” #

This site is a shadcn registry at /3.0/r/. npx shadcn@latest add copies a file into your project, adds the npm dependencies, and merges the theme:

  • A React wrapper per component family, such as md-button or md-menu (a menu with its group and item). The file is components/ui/md-<name>.tsx. It registers the md-gb-* elements and wraps each one with @lit/react: typed props from the element class, and the events as onChange, onClose and so on.
  • md-theme, installed with every item: it loads the M3 styles and maps your shadcn variables to the M3 color and shape roles.
  • md-theme-m3, optional: the reverse, the M3 baseline as shadcn variables, so shadcn components match the md-gb elements.

The registry lists every item in registry.json.

Add a component

Link to “Add a component” #

The plain URL form needs no setup:

npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-button.json

To use the short form, add the registry to components.json once. The keys of registries start with @, and {name} is the item:

{
  "registries": {
    "@material-web": "https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
 
npx shadcn@latest add @material-web/md-button @material-web/md-menu

The command installs @material/web and @lit/react with your package manager. Each component page has this command after its first example.

Use the component like any other. The JSON and TSX blocks on this page are plain blocks and not live demos: the TSX needs React, which this page does not load, and the JSON is configuration with no visible effect.

import {MdButton} from '@/components/ui/md-button';
import {MdMenu, MdMenuItem} from '@/components/ui/md-menu';

export function Actions() {
  return (
    <>
      <MdButton color="filled" popoverTarget="file-menu">
        File
      </MdButton>
      <MdMenu id="file-menu">
        <MdMenuItem onChange={(event) => console.log(event.type)}>Open</MdMenuItem>
      </MdMenu>
    </>
  );
}

The theme bridge

Link to “The theme bridge” #

md-theme adds @import "@material/web/labs/gb/styles/m3.css" to your global CSS, then declares the --md-sys-* variables in :root and in .dark from your shadcn variables. The M3 styles are in a cascade layer and the bridge is not, so the bridge wins regardless of the order of the imports. Change your shadcn theme, or toggle .dark, and the elements follow. It also sets color-scheme for :root and .dark.

Containers stay with their on- colors: each pair maps to a pair that shadcn already keeps readable together. The *-fixed roles, scrim and shadow keep the M3 baseline.

M3 role shadcn value Why
--md-sys-color-primary var(--primary) Same role.
--md-sys-color-on-primary var(--primary-foreground) Same pair.
--md-sys-color-primary-container var(--accent) shadcn has no primary container; accent is its tinted fill.
--md-sys-color-on-primary-container var(--accent-foreground) Pairs with accent.
--md-sys-color-secondary var(--muted-foreground) The mid-tone solid; text on it is --background.
--md-sys-color-on-secondary var(--background) Pairs with the solid above.
--md-sys-color-secondary-container var(--secondary) shadcn secondary is a tonal fill, like an M3 container.
--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container var(--secondary-foreground) Pairs with secondary.
--md-sys-color-tertiary var(--primary) shadcn has no tertiary; it follows primary.
--md-sys-color-on-tertiary var(--primary-foreground) Pairs with primary.
--md-sys-color-tertiary-container var(--accent) Follows the primary container.
--md-sys-color-on-tertiary-container var(--accent-foreground) Pairs with accent.
--md-sys-color-error var(--destructive) Same role.
--md-sys-color-on-error var(--destructive-foreground, oklch(1 0 0)) shadcn v4 has no destructive-foreground; white.
--md-sys-color-error-container color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 14%, var(--background)) A tint of destructive on the background.
--md-sys-color-on-error-container var(--destructive) Destructive on its tint.
--md-sys-color-background var(--background) Same role.
--md-sys-color-on-background var(--foreground) Same pair.
--md-sys-color-surface var(--background) The page surface.
--md-sys-color-on-surface var(--foreground) Same pair.
--md-sys-color-surface-variant var(--muted) Muted fill.
--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant var(--muted-foreground) Muted text.
--md-sys-color-surface-tint var(--primary) Same as primary.
--md-sys-color-surface-dim var(--muted) Muted fill.
--md-sys-color-surface-bright var(--background) The page surface.
--md-sys-color-surface-container-lowest var(--background) Lowest tone: the page.
--md-sys-color-surface-container-low var(--card) Cards.
--md-sys-color-surface-container var(--popover) Menus and popovers.
--md-sys-color-surface-container-high var(--muted) Muted fill.
--md-sys-color-surface-container-highest var(--accent) Accent fill (the highest tone in both schemes).
--md-sys-color-outline var(--muted-foreground) M3 needs 3:1 against the surface; shadcn --border is too faint for field and button outlines.
--md-sys-color-outline-variant var(--border) Dividers and decorative borders.
--md-sys-color-inverse-surface var(--foreground) Inverse of the page.
--md-sys-color-inverse-on-surface var(--background) Pairs with the inverse surface.
--md-sys-color-inverse-primary var(--primary-foreground) Primary-side color that reads on the inverse surface.

Corners follow --radius (the px values are the M3 ones at shadcn's default 0.625rem). --md-sys-shape-corner-value-* get the same values.

M3 corner shadcn value
--md-sys-shape-corner-xs calc(var(--radius) * 0.4)
--md-sys-shape-corner-sm calc(var(--radius) * 0.8)
--md-sys-shape-corner-md calc(var(--radius) * 1.2)
--md-sys-shape-corner-lg calc(var(--radius) * 1.6)
--md-sys-shape-corner-lg-increased calc(var(--radius) * 2)
--md-sys-shape-corner-xl calc(var(--radius) * 2.8)
--md-sys-shape-corner-xl-increased calc(var(--radius) * 3.2)
--md-sys-shape-corner-xxl calc(var(--radius) * 4.8)

shadcn has no tertiary role, so it follows primary. outline is the muted foreground and not --border, because M3 needs 3:1 against the surface for the outline of a field or an outlined button; --border is the outline-variant (dividers).

Match shadcn to the M3 baseline

Link to “Match shadcn to the M3 baseline” #

md-theme-m3 goes the other way. It writes the baseline colors of M3 (light and dark) into the shadcn variables:

npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-theme-m3.json
shadcn variable M3 baseline role
--background --md-sys-color-surface
--foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface
--card --md-sys-color-surface-container-low
--card-foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface
--popover --md-sys-color-surface-container
--popover-foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface
--primary --md-sys-color-primary
--primary-foreground --md-sys-color-on-primary
--secondary --md-sys-color-secondary-container
--secondary-foreground --md-sys-color-on-secondary-container
--muted --md-sys-color-surface-container-high
--muted-foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface-variant
--accent --md-sys-color-surface-container-highest
--accent-foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface
--destructive --md-sys-color-error
--border --md-sys-color-outline-variant
--input --md-sys-color-outline
--ring --md-sys-color-primary
--chart-1 --md-sys-color-primary
--chart-2 --md-sys-color-tertiary
--chart-3 --md-sys-color-secondary
--chart-4 --md-sys-color-primary-fixed-dim
--chart-5 --md-sys-color-tertiary-fixed-dim
--sidebar --md-sys-color-surface-container-low
--sidebar-foreground --md-sys-color-on-surface
--sidebar-primary --md-sys-color-primary
--sidebar-primary-foreground --md-sys-color-on-primary
--sidebar-accent --md-sys-color-secondary-container
--sidebar-accent-foreground --md-sys-color-on-secondary-container
--sidebar-border --md-sys-color-outline-variant
--sidebar-ring --md-sys-color-primary

--radius is 0.75rem, the M3 medium corner.

It is independent of md-theme. With both installed, the bridge points the M3 roles at shadcn variables that now hold the M3 colors, so the two agree.

Bundler setup

Link to “Bundler setup” #

The elements import their styles as CSS module scripts (import styles from './menu.css' with {type: 'css'}). Browsers support that, but Vite, webpack and Node do not without help, and the build fails with "default" is not exported by "…/focus-ring.css". Every stylesheet ships next to a Lit CSSResult module (menu.cssresult.js), so a one-time plugin that points the imports there is enough. For Vite (a plain block; it is configuration with no visible effect):

// vite.config.ts
import {defineConfig, type Plugin} from 'vite';

function mdGbCssModules(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: 'md-gb-css-modules',
    enforce: 'pre',
    transform(code, id) {
      if (!/[\\/]@material[\\/]web[\\/]/.test(id) || !id.endsWith('.js')) return;
      return code.replace(
        /import\s+(\w+)\s+from\s+'(\.[^']*)\.css'\s+with\s*\{\s*type:\s*'css'\s*\};?/g,
        "import {styles as $1} from '$2.cssresult.js';",
      );
    },
  };
}

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [mdGbCssModules() /* , react(), tailwindcss() */],
  optimizeDeps: {exclude: ['@material/web']},
});

Limits

Link to “Limits” #
  • Tailwind classes style only the host. The elements use shadow DOM, so className="bg-red-500" colors the <md-gb-button> box, not its inside. Customize with the --md-* custom properties and ::part() selectors listed in each component's API reference. They work in a plain CSS file or in Tailwind's arbitrary properties, such as [--container-color:red].
  • Client only. The wrappers start with 'use client', and the elements cannot be imported in Node (they use CSS module scripts, customElements and document). In Next.js the server renders client components too, so import the file with next/dynamic(() => import('...'), {ssr: false}) or render it after mount, unless you set up Lit SSR.
  • Labs. The elements come from @material/web/labs/gb/. The registry keeps @material/web as the dependency, and the path needs a version that ships labs/gb.
  • Typography, motion and icons are not bridged. Load the Material Symbols font as in the quick start.
  • Local testing. When this site runs from the dev server the registry files point to http://localhost:8000. Set MWC_REGISTRY_URL to build them for another origin.

The registry files are generated by scripts/m3/gb-shadcn.mjs from the element sources, so the props and events match the API reference. For agents, the same information is in llms.txt and custom-elements.json.

Theming

Material Design theming creates unique branded products with familiar patterns and accessible interactions.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/design-tokens/

Tokens

Link to “Tokens” #

Material is expressed in design tokens, which are the building blocks of all UI elements.

In 3.0, the md-gb-* elements are themed with system tokens, which map roles to concrete reference values. Load them once for the document with adoptStyles(), then override any token with CSS.

System tokens are CSS custom properties in the md.sys.* cascade layers, so unlayered CSS always wins and they can be scoped with any selector.

System

Link to “System” #

System tokens define the decisions and roles that give the design system its character: color, typography, shape, elevation, space, and motion.

Color

Link to “Color” #

--md-sys-color tokens define the dynamic color roles. They use light-dark(), so they follow color-scheme. See the color guide.

Typography

Link to “Typography” #

--md-sys-typescale tokens define the type scale, including the emphasized styles. See the typography guide.

Shape

Link to “Shape” #

--md-sys-shape tokens define the corner scale, including single-corner values. See the shape guide.

Motion

Link to “Motion” #

--md-sys-motion tokens define the motion scheme: spring tokens (--md-sys-motion-spring-<speed>-<spatial|effects>, each with a matching -duration), easing curves, and durations. Springs are linear() easings. The standard scheme applies to elements inside .md-motion-standard.

Component

Link to “Component” #

The md-gb-* elements do not expose per-component tokens. Change how a component looks by changing the system tokens it uses (color roles, typescale styles, shape corners, motion), by scoping them to a selector, or with the component's attributes such as variant and size.

Interaction States

Interactive components show their state with a state layer: a translucent overlay of the component's content color, drawn between the container and the content.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/interaction-states/

Interactive components show their state with a state layer: a translucent overlay of the component's content color, drawn between the container and the content. Components handle this for you. You only need to know which state shows which layer.

State Layer opacity When
Hover 8% A cursor rests over the element (hover-capable input)
Focus 10% Keyboard or voice focus
Pressed 10% A tap or click is in progress
Dragged 16% The element is being dragged

Hover and focus combine. A focused, hovered element shows the focus layer too. Disabled components show no state layers: they cannot be focused, dragged or pressed, and they do not inherit hover.

Hover only where it is real

Link to “Hover only where it is real” #

Hover applies only on devices that can hover, through @media (hover: hover). A tap on a touch screen does not leave the hover layer on. Do not hide essential content or controls behind hover, because touch users never see it.

Pressed ripple

Link to “Pressed ripple” #

The pressed state plays a ripple, with this timing:

  • The layer fades in over 75ms.
  • The circle grows over 225ms (fast-out, slow-in), while its center moves to the middle.
  • Once the press is released and the growth is done, the layer fades out over 150ms.

A quick tap still shows the ripple for at least 225ms, so a press always reads as a press.

Use the ripple as written. Do not add a second press effect on top of it.

Usage

Link to “Usage” #

Components apply their states on their own. Use them like any other element.

Watch out for

Link to “Watch out for” #
  • Do not restyle the state layer colors per screen. The opacities are part of the state, so keep them as they are.
  • Do not tell people to "hover to see" an action. Show it, or give it a visible label.
  • Keep focus visible. The focus layer is not a replacement for the focus ring.

Accessibility

Every labs/gb component works with a keyboard, a screen reader and reduced motion.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/accessibility/

The rules below are the ones the components follow and the tests check.

Keyboard

Link to “Keyboard” #

Composite components (button groups, chip sets, lists, menus, tabs, navigation, pickers) share one roving focus model in labs/gb/components/shared/roving-focus.ts:

  • Arrow keys move between items along the orientation. Left and Right follow the reading direction, so they mirror in RTL.
  • Home and End go to the first and last item. Focus wraps at the ends unless the component turns wrapping off.
  • Disabled items are skipped. Soft-disabled items stay focusable.
  • Only one item is in the tab order at a time (roving tabindex). Tab enters the group on the item that was focused last, or the first one.
  • Keys pressed with Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift are left to the browser.

Escape clears keyboard focus: it hides the focus indicator and starts the focus order over, so Tab after Escape reaches the first focusable element again. In a text field, Escape removes the cursor and keeps the typed text. If a handler already used the Escape key, the component leaves it alone.

A dialog fires cancel on Escape, a scrim click or the full-screen close button. Canceling keeps the dialog open if you call preventDefault():

Focus ring

Link to “Focus ring” #

The focus ring is drawn with outline, using the --focus-ring-outline and --focus-ring-offset variables from labs/gb/components/focus/focus-ring.scss. The thickness, color and offsets come from the state focus indicator tokens, so a theme changes them in one place. Do not remove the outline with CSS unless you draw a replacement that passes the same tests.

Screen readers and ARIA

Link to “Screen readers and ARIA” #

Components use WAI-ARIA 1.3 roles, states and properties. The model of the draft and the checks that report misuse live in labs/gb/components/shared/central/aria_test.ts. Axe-core runs against every component in labs/gb/components/shared/central/axe_test.ts, so a missing label or an invalid attribute fails the suite.

Material Design 3 wins where it and WAI-ARIA 1.3 disagree. In every other case the ARIA rules apply as written. When you add a component, follow the M3 page for its behavior first, then check the ARIA role and attributes it uses.

Reduced motion

Link to “Reduced motion” #

Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The motion helpers in labs/gb/components/shared/motion.ts resolve to 0 ms under that setting and inside an ancestor with the md-motion-reduced class. The motion tokens in labs/gb/styles/motion/ follow the same rule. Ripples skip the animated press and show their end state, and the effect tokens (color, opacity, shape) do not change.

Do not animate with hard-coded durations. Read the duration from the motion helpers or the tokens, so reduced motion applies to your component too.

Adaptive layout

Pages and components change with the window.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/adaptive-layout/

labs/gb uses the M3 window size classes to pick the navigation, the number of panes and how dialogs open.

Window size classes

Link to “Window size classes” #
Class Width (CSS px)
compact below 600
medium 600 to 839
expanded 840 to 1199
large 1200 to 1599
extra-large 1600 and up

Height classes are compact (below 480), medium (480 to 899) and expanded (900 and up). Most layouts scroll, so only use the height class when a component needs it.

A component gets its class from AdaptiveController in labs/gb/components/shared/adaptive.ts. The controller sets the window-size-class attribute on the host, so CSS can match it. Options are keyed by class and apply from that class up. Match the attribute in CSS and use atLeast('expanded') in code. Do not read the window width directly.

In a Lit element, create the controller as a field and read options in render(). This sample uses a plain element as the host, so it runs without Lit:

App scaffold

Link to “App scaffold” #

md-gb-app-scaffold lays out the bars and rails around the app's content:

  • A navigation bar at compact, a navigation rail at medium and larger.
  • At medium, a navigation bar is used instead when a nested md-gb-pane-scaffold shows two panes, unless the window height is compact.
  • A companion rail sits on the trailing side at large and extra-large.
  • A toolbar floats in the bottom rail region at compact.
  • The FAB sits 16 px from the trailing and bottom edges of the content, and the snackbar sits above it.

Provide both a md-gb-nav-bar and a md-gb-nav-rail with the same destinations, and keep their selection in sync. The scaffold shows only one of them.

Panes

Link to “Panes” #

md-gb-pane-scaffold shows one, two or three panes. The default slot is the primary (flexible) pane, secondary is the list of a list-detail layout, and tertiary is an optional third pane, such as a standard side sheet. placeholder is shown in the primary pane of a two-pane layout with nothing selected.

Safe areas

Link to “Safe areas” #

The scaffold keeps its bars away from the device safe areas. It reads --md-gb-scaffold-safe-top, -right, -bottom and -left, which default to env(safe-area-inset-*). Keep primary content out of those edges. To change the insets, set the custom properties on the scaffold.

Full-screen dialogs

Link to “Full-screen dialogs” #

A full-screen dialog is for compact windows only. Set full-screen on md-gb-dialog: at compact it fills the window, and at medium and larger it falls back to a basic dialog with the same slots. Set always-full-screen to keep the full-screen variant at every size, if the task needs it.

Density

Density lets people see more information in data-heavy views by making components more compact.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/density/

Density lets people see more information in data-heavy views by making components more compact. A component's density is a number from 0 (the default) to -3 (the densest). Each step down makes the component smaller. Values are rounded and clamped to that range.

Use the density attribute.

Which components support it

Link to “Which components support it” #

density is available on these components:

  • md-gb-button-group
  • md-gb-checkbox
  • md-gb-chip
  • md-gb-icon-button
  • md-gb-list
  • md-gb-menu
  • md-gb-radio
  • md-gb-segmented-button
  • md-gb-switch
  • md-gb-tabs
  • md-gb-text-field
  • md-gb-time-picker

Each step shrinks the component's visual size, not its touch target. A checkbox, for example, loses 4px from its layout box (48px at density 0) and its state layer (40px at density 0) per step. Its touch target stays 48px.

Touch targets stay 48dp

Link to “Touch targets stay 48dp” #

Every component keeps a touch target of at least 48 by 48 CSS pixels, even at the densest setting. The visual element can be smaller, but the area that responds to a tap cannot. Do not override this with your own sizing.

Rules of thumb

Link to “Rules of thumb” #
  • Density is a choice, not a default. Leave components at 0 unless the view is data-heavy, and let people opt into a denser layout where you offer a control for it.
  • Do not change density automatically. It should not switch when the window resizes or the device rotates, unless the person changed it.
  • Consider the device. A person may want a dense desktop layout but not a dense phone layout.
  • Layout density comes first. Spacing changes can add information without shrinking components. Use component density when you also need the controls themselves to be smaller.
  • Keep the controls accessible. If you offer a density setting, the setting itself must be easy to find and use.

Layout

Layout adapts an app to the window with window size classes, a column grid, margins and panes.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/layout/

Layout adapts an app to the window. The window size class (see Adaptive layout) sets the layout tokens on :root:

  • --md-sys-layout-columns: 4 at compact, 8 at medium and expanded, 12 from large up.
  • --md-sys-layout-margin: 16px at compact, 24px above.
  • --md-sys-layout-spacer: the gutter between columns, 16px at compact, 24px above.

Window size classes and grid

Link to “Window size classes and grid” #

.md-layout-grid lays its children out on the column grid, with the margin as inline padding and the spacer as the gap.

Add .md-window to an element so its direct children follow that element's width instead of the viewport.

To react in code, observe the class of the window or of an element:

Foldables

Link to “Foldables” #

On a foldable device, the fold's position and size are available as --md-sys-layout-fold-left and --md-sys-layout-fold-width (vertical fold) or --md-sys-layout-fold-top and --md-sys-layout-fold-height (horizontal fold). To react in code, observe the fold. The callback gets null when there is none.

Scaffold

A scaffold arranges the bars, rails and panes around an app's content, and adapts them to the window size.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/foundations/scaffold/

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Structure the app in bars, rails and panes. Bars frame the page, rails run along its edges, and panes hold the content.
  • Provide both navigation components. Give the scaffold a navigation bar and a navigation rail with the same destinations. It shows the bar in compact windows and the rail from medium windows up, and you keep their selection in sync.
  • Pick the pane layout by content. Use list-detail for a collection and its details, supporting pane for a focus area with related content, and feed for a grid of items.
  • Use one to three panes. The number of visible panes follows the window size.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

md-gb-app-scaffold places bars and rails around its content. md-gb-pane-scaffold goes in the content and arranges the panes.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

List-detail

Link to “List-detail” #

The default layout shows a list in the secondary slot and its detail in the default slot. In windows with one pane they take turns: call openDetail() when someone picks an item and closeDetail() from a back button. The placeholder slot fills the detail pane until one is open.

Supporting pane

Link to “Supporting pane” #

Set layout="supporting-pane" for a focus area in the default slot with related content in the secondary slot, at the trailing side by default.

Feed

Link to “Feed” #

Set layout="feed" to lay the default slot's items out on a grid, with an optional secondary pane beside it.

Resizable panes

Link to “Resizable panes” #

Add resizable to a two-pane layout to show a drag handle between the panes. pane-width sets the width of the secondary pane in pixels, and collapsed-pane records a pane collapsed with the handle. The scaffold fires pane-resize when the panes change size.

Floating and docked panes

Link to “Floating and docked panes” #

When there is no room for a supporting pane beside the content, set levitate to floating or docked to lift the secondary pane above it instead of stacking it below. A docked pane sits at the bottom edge on compact windows, like a bottom sheet. Open it with openLevitated() and close it with closeLevitated(). Add levitate-modal for a scrim, and levitate-label to name the pane.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Give each navigation component an aria-label, such as "Primary navigation", and keep the bar and rail selections in sync.
  • In a single-pane list-detail layout, provide a back button that calls closeDetail().
  • A modal levitated pane takes focus, closes with Escape and when someone uses the content behind it, and is named by levitate-label.
  • A floating pane's move and resize handles also work with the arrow keys. Use drag-handle-label, levitate-move-label and levitate-resize-label to translate their names.

API reference

Link to “API reference” #

<md-gb-app-scaffold>

Link to “<md-gb-app-scaffold>” #

A Material Design app scaffold (bars, rails, FAB, snackbar).

Properties

Link to “Properties” #
Property Attribute Type Default
autoExpandRail
Whether to expand a slotted navigation rail at large and extra-large windows and collapse it below (spec: breakpoints, swapping components). Applied when the window size class changes.		 auto-expand-rail boolean false
navigation
Which navigation component to show.		 navigation ScaffoldNavigation 'auto'
sideSheetNavigation
What the navigation rail does while a side sheet is present (spec: breakpoints and scaffold): keep it as is, collapse it to the collapsed rail, or hide it completely. A side sheet is present while the nested pane scaffold shows its tertiary pane or side-sheet-open is set.		 side-sheet-navigation SideSheetNavigation 'keep'
sideSheetOpen
Whether an app-managed side sheet is open.		 side-sheet-open boolean false

Slots

Link to “Slots” #
Slot Description
default The content, typically an md-gb-pane-scaffold. Scrolls.
companion-rail A companion rail on the trailing side of large and extra-large windows, holding supporting controls or actions that modify or relate to the content in a pane.
fab A FAB, 16px from the trailing and bottom edges of the content.
navigation-bar A navigation bar (md-gb-nav-bar) at the bottom.
navigation-rail A navigation rail (md-gb-nav-rail) at the leading edge.
snackbar A snackbar host (md-gb-snackbar), above the FAB.
toolbar A toolbar floating in the bottom rail region, centered above the navigation bar (mobile).
top-app-bar A top app bar (md-gb-app-bar), beside the rail.

CustomEvent<NavigationChangeDetail>		 Fired when the shown navigation component changes.

::part(companion-rail) The companion rail region.

<md-gb-pane-scaffold>

Link to “<md-gb-pane-scaffold>” #

A Material Design pane scaffold (list-detail, supporting pane, feed).

Properties

Link to “Properties” #
Property Attribute Type Default
arrangement
How two panes share the width.		 arrangement PaneArrangement 'fixed-flexible'
collapsedPane
A pane collapsed with the drag handle, or null.		 collapsed-pane "primary" "secondary"
detailOpen
List-detail: whether an item is selected. Single-pane windows show the detail (primary) pane when true and the list (secondary) pane when false; two-pane windows show the placeholder slot instead of the detail while false.		 detail-open boolean false
dragHandleLabel
Accessible label of the drag handle.		 drag-handle-label string 'Resize panes'
handleTap
What a tap, Enter or Space on the drag handle does, the single-pointer alternative to dragging it: toggle (default) switches between one and two panes; cycle steps through the snap widths and then collapses the secondary pane.		 handle-tap PaneHandleTap 'toggle'
layout
The canonical layout.		 layout PaneScaffoldLayout 'list-detail'
levitate
The levitate strategy for the secondary pane of supporting pane and feed layouts in windows too small for two panes: none reflows it below the primary pane, floating floats it above, docked docks it to the bottom edge at compact (floating from medium).		 levitate PaneLevitate 'none'
levitateCoplanar
Keeps a levitated pane co-planar at large and extra-large windows. By default it floats there (spec: scaffold, "On large screens: floating panes are the default").		 levitate-coplanar boolean false
levitateDraggable
Lets a floating pane be dragged by its handle, or moved with the arrow keys while the handle is focused (spec: scaffold, floating panes "can be customized to be dragged or resized").		 levitate-draggable boolean false
levitateLabel
Accessible label of a modal levitated pane (its dialog role).		 levitate-label string ''
levitateModal
Whether the levitated secondary pane is modal (scrim, inert panes).		 levitate-modal boolean false
levitateMoveLabel
Accessible label of the floating pane's move handle.		 levitate-move-label string 'Move pane'
levitateOpen
Whether the levitated secondary pane is shown.		 levitate-open boolean false
levitateResizable
Lets a floating pane be resized by its corner handle, or with the arrow keys while the handle is focused.		 levitate-resizable boolean false
levitateResizeLabel
Accessible label of the floating pane's resize handle.		 levitate-resize-label string 'Resize pane'
mediumTwoPane
Whether medium windows show two panes (50% each) instead of one. The spec limits this to low-density content such as settings.		 medium-two-pane boolean false
paneWidth
Width in px of the secondary pane set with the drag handle, or null for the default width. Set it to restore a persisted width.		 pane-width number null
resizable
Whether two-pane layouts render a drag handle to resize the panes.		 resizable boolean false
resizeBehavior
persistent keeps a resized width or collapsed pane across window size class changes; temporary returns to the default layout. Defaults to persistent for list-detail and temporary for the other layouts.		 resize-behavior PaneResizeBehavior undefined
scrollLabel
Accessible label of the stacked panes' scroll region. Only used while the stacked panes overflow and hold nothing focusable: the region is then focusable (so the keyboard can scroll it) and a labelled region.		 scroll-label string 'Panes'
secondaryPosition
Where the secondary pane sits in two-pane layouts. Defaults to start for list-detail and end for supporting pane and feed layouts. Mirrors in right-to-left.		 secondary-position PanePosition undefined

Slots

Link to “Slots” #
Slot Description
default The primary (flexible) pane: the detail pane of a list-detail layout, the focus pane of a supporting pane layout, or the feed items (laid out on a grid) of a feed layout.
placeholder Shown in the primary pane of a two-pane list-detail layout while detail-open is false (no item selected). Levitate (spec: scaffold, "Levitate"): with levitate="floating" or levitate="docked", the secondary pane of a supporting pane or feed layout floats above the primary pane (or docks to the bottom edge at compact, like a bottom sheet) in windows too small for two co-planar panes, while levitate-open is set. levitate-modal makes it modal: a scrim covers the panes, the primary pane is inert, focus moves into the pane and back to the trigger, and the pane closes when something behind it is used or Escape is pressed. Modality is scoped to the scaffold; use md-gb-dialog or md-gb-sheet for app-wide modals. At large and extra-large windows a levitated pane keeps floating (spec: "On large screens, floating panes are the default"); the scrim is optional (levitate-modal adds it). levitate-coplanar opts into a co-planar pane there instead. levitate-draggable and levitate-resizable add a move handle and a resize corner to a floating pane: drag them, or focus them and use the arrow keys (Shift moves in larger steps). levitate-change fires after each move or resize. Foldables: the scaffold reads the fold (hinge) from the Viewport Segments API and keeps panes off it. A vertical fold splits two panes at the fold with the spacer on it (at least the spacer width); a horizontal fold (tabletop) stacks the supporting pane below it. The fold crossing the scaffold is reflected as the fold attribute (vertical or horizontal). Browsers without the API keep the regular layout.
secondary The secondary pane: the list of a list-detail layout or the supporting pane. It is the fixed pane in fixed-and-flexible arrangements.
tertiary An optional third pane (e.g. a standard side sheet), shown at extra-large only.

Event		 Fired when the scaffold closes a levitated pane (Escape, or using something behind a modal pane).
pane-layout-change
CustomEvent<PaneLayoutChangeDetail>		 Fired when the visible panes change.
pane-resize
CustomEvent<PaneResizeDetail>		 Fired when the panes are resized or collapsed with the drag handle.
window-class-change
CustomEvent<WindowClassChangeDetail>		 Fired when the window size class changes.
window-height-class-change
CustomEvent<WindowHeightClassChangeDetail>		 Fired when the window height size class changes.
