Color

Color creates meaning and communicates hierarchy, state, and brand.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/color/

Color scheme

Link to “Color scheme” #

The page follows the subpages of the M3 color guidance in order. All imports come from @material/web/labs/gb/styles/color/.

Color system

Link to “Color system” #

The system turns a few inputs into a complete, accessible set of colors. Dynamic color starts from a source color, runs it through a scheme algorithm, derives five key colors (primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral, neutral variant) plus error, builds a tonal palette for each in HCT (hue, chroma, tone), and assigns tones to color roles. Roles come with a pairing rule: a color and its on- color are chosen so text and icons stay legible. Each role has three contrast levels (standard, medium, high), so the same scheme can serve people who need more contrast.

In labs/gb:

  • md-color-tokens.css is the static baseline: every role as a --md-sys-color-<role> custom property, with light and dark values.
  • md-color-tokens-contrast.css adds medium and high contrast. High contrast follows prefers-contrast: more, and .md-contrast-standard, .md-contrast-medium and .md-contrast-high select a level for a subtree.
  • md-color-tokens-full.css also declares the reference palette (--md-ref-palette-*), the tonal palettes the roles are picked from.
  • dynamic-color.ts runs the generation steps at runtime with Material Color Utilities (see Dynamic color below).

The new tone-based surface roles (container levels, dim, and bright) and the fixed accent roles from the latest spec are all part of the tokens, so nothing extra is needed to use them. HCT is also available as a small API (see Advanced customization).

Color roles

Link to “Color roles” #

A role is a named job for a color, not a specific hue. Components read roles (primary, surface-container) instead of hex values, so a new scheme re-themes everything. The spec groups them as accent roles (primary, secondary, tertiary, error, each with on-, -container and on-container variants), surface roles with on-surface and on-surface-variant, outline roles, inverse roles, and add-on roles: fixed accents and bright and dim surfaces. Layer from lower to higher emphasis, and always put on- content on its matching background.

Role Tokens
Primary, secondary, tertiary --md-sys-color-<accent>, -on-<accent>, -<accent>-container, -on-<accent>-container
Fixed accents --md-sys-color-<accent>-fixed, -<accent>-fixed-dim, -on-<accent>-fixed, -on-<accent>-fixed-variant
Error --md-sys-color-error, -on-error, -error-container, -on-error-container
Surface --md-sys-color-surface, -surface-dim, -surface-bright, -surface-container-lowest through -surface-container-highest, -on-surface, -on-surface-variant
Outline --md-sys-color-outline, -outline-variant
Inverse --md-sys-color-inverse-surface, -inverse-on-surface, -inverse-primary
Other --md-sys-color-scrim, -shadow

Fixed accents keep the same value in light and dark themes, for content that should not flip, such as a brand surface. Use surface-dim and surface-bright for areas that stay darker or brighter than the main surface in both themes.

Light and dark

Link to “Light and dark” #

The tokens use light-dark(), so they follow the standard color-scheme property. Where light-dark() is not available, the Baseline fallback keeps the light values and switches to the dark values with prefers-color-scheme.

The deprecated background and surface-tint roles are not defined; use surface and a surface container instead.

Choosing a scheme

Link to “Choosing a scheme” #

Pick static color when you want a fixed, predictable palette: a brand identity, a product with a strict visual identity, or a small, controlled UI. Pick dynamic color when the palette should come from the person or the content: a wallpaper, a profile color, an album cover. You can also mix both: a dynamic scheme for most of the UI and static colors for brand and semantic meaning.

In labs/gb that is a choice of which stylesheet or function you load:

  • Static: import md-color-tokens.css (and md-color-tokens-contrast.css if you want contrast levels). No JavaScript.
  • Dynamic: call themeFromSource(), themeFromImage() or applyTheme(), which output the same custom properties and override the static ones.

Static color

Link to “Static color” #

The spec has two kinds. Baseline is the default purple scheme, ready to use and a good starting point for prototypes. Custom brand keeps the same roles but replaces the key colors with your brand colors, usually exported from the Material Theme Builder or a design tool.

Baseline in labs/gb is the default stylesheet. It is also part of m3Styles, which adoptStyles() loads.

For a custom brand scheme, override the tokens by hand, or generate the roles once and keep the CSS.

To start from a Material Theme Builder export, pass its JSON to themeFromThemeBuilder(), or apply it live with themeOptionsFromThemeBuilder().

The seed (or the core primary) is the source, other core colors become palettes, extended colors become harmonized or exact customColors, and a variant or contrast field in the file is used if present. The generated schemes and palettes in the export are ignored, so the roles match the rest of labs/gb. A second argument overrides any option.

Dynamic color

Link to “Dynamic color” #

A dynamic scheme is generated from a source. The spec distinguishes user-generated color (a wallpaper or a person's pick, usually with the tonal-spot variant), content-based color (taken from an image or content on screen, with the content variant), and multiple sources (several schemes on one screen, each scoped to a region).

For content-based color, scope the scheme to one element with a source taken from an image:

To get the theme without applying it, use themeFromSource() or themeFromImage(img), and themeToStyleSheet(theme) for a stylesheet.

  • Variants: tonal-spot, neutral, vibrant, expressive, fidelity, content, monochrome, rainbow, and fruit-salad. The spec page does not define these variants or any version of their rules; they come from Material Color Utilities, which has 2025 rules only for tonal spot, neutral, vibrant and expressive. The others use the original rules, so labs/gb does too. theme.specVersion reports what was used.
  • Contrast: standard, medium, high, or a number from -1 to 1. applyTheme() accepts contrast: 'auto', which uses high contrast when the user prefers more contrast.
  • Platform: phone (also right for the web) or watch.
  • applyTheme(target, ...) accepts a document, a shadow root, or an element. An element gets inline custom properties, so its subtree has its own scheme. clearTheme() removes it.
  • Android's system-wide wallpaper source and the Material Theme Builder preview are not part of labs/gb; the library only generates the scheme.

When using content-based color, keep semantic colors (error, success) stable and make sure the surrounding UI stays readable if the image is very saturated or very dark. The scheme already guarantees accessible on-color pairs.

Advanced customization

Link to “Advanced customization” #

The spec lists three kinds of customization. This table shows what labs/gb covers.

Spec topic In labs/gb
Combine multiple color schemes Yes: call applyTheme(element, ...) on different elements, each with its own source, variant and contrast.
Map or remap colors on UI elements Yes: components read roles, so reassign a role in CSS (--md-sys-color-surface: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container);) on a subtree.
Define static colors Yes: customColors adds a color with four roles.
Define custom color roles Yes: customRoles takes a name, a palette and a tone for light and dark (optionally per contrast level).
Define your own baseline scheme Yes: override the static tokens, or pass palettes.
Define your own dynamic scheme Yes: palettes takes your own primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral, neutral variant and error key colors.
Use color fidelity Yes: fidelity per role.
Harmonize colors Yes: customColors harmonize toward the source by default, and harmonize(color, source) is exported.

Harmonize colors that carry meaning but should still sit in the theme, such as success and warning. Do not harmonize brand colors that must stay exact.

Custom color roles

Link to “Custom color roles” #

A custom role is one color picked from a palette at a reference tone, for light and dark, so it follows the source color and the contrast level like the built-in roles. It makes --md-sys-color-<name> only; pick a tone that meets contrast against the role it sits on (3:1 for graphics) and check the pair yourself.

palette is one of primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral, neutralVariant, error. Tones are 0 to 100; a number applies to both themes.

HCT

Link to “HCT” #

Colors in the system are built in HCT (hue, chroma, tone). To work in it yourself:

Colors outside the sRGB range are brought in by lowering chroma.

Prefer an existing role before adding custom colors, and keep contrast pairs accessible; customColors roles follow the same on-color convention as the accents.

Resources

Link to “Resources” #

The spec's resources page links to the Material Theme Builder, the Figma plugin, and tutorials and codelabs. For code:

  • Material Theme Builder Figma plugin to design a scheme and export tokens.
  • material-color-utilities, the library dynamic-color.ts is built on.
  • Color on m3.material.io for the full guidance.

Dynamic color

Dynamic color builds a full color scheme, light and dark, from a seed color.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/dynamic-color/

Dynamic color turns one source color into every color role, in light and dark. Pick a source and a variant, and apply the result to the document or to one element.

Scheme variants

Link to “Scheme variants” #

The variant decides how the palettes are derived from the source: tonal-spot (the default), neutral, vibrant, expressive, fidelity, content, monochrome, rainbow and fruit-salad.

Contrast levels

Link to “Contrast levels” #

Each scheme has standard, medium and high contrast. Set contrast on applyTheme(), or select a level for a subtree of the static tokens with a class.

See Color for roles, custom colors and the full options.

Typography

Typography helps make writing legible and beautiful.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/typography/

Tip: "typeface" and "typescale" can be confusing. "face" refers to font-family and font-weight.

"scale" refers to a group of font-family, font-size, line-height, and font-weight tokens.

Typeface

Link to “Typeface” #

A typeface is a font-family. In Material there are plain and brand typefaces.

Each typeface has normal, medium, and bold styles (defaults to 400, 500, and 700). All three weight styles need to be included for a font.

Important: the default typeface is Roboto Flex, then Roboto. If you do not change it, load one of them. For example, from fonts.google.com.

Tokens

Link to “Tokens” #

Typefaces can be set using CSS custom properties. Tokens follow the naming convention --md-ref-typeface-<token>.

Typeface Token
Brand --md-ref-typeface-brand
Plain --md-ref-typeface-plain
  • All tokens

Typescale

Link to “Typescale” #

A typescale is a collection of font styles: font-family, font-size, line-height, and font-weight. They are organized into roles that describe their purpose.

Material's applying type guidelines explains when to use each typescale role.

Classes

Link to “Classes” #

The type scale is applied with the font shorthand tokens and their -axes and -tracking companions, which also work inside shadow roots.

Tokens

Link to “Tokens” #

The scale has five roles (display, headline, title, body, label), each in sm, md, and lg, plus emphasized styles per role. Tokens follow --md-sys-typescale-<role>-<size>-<property> with the properties font, size, line-height, weight, tracking, and axes; the bare --md-sys-typescale-<role>-<size> is the combined font shorthand.

Typescale Tokens
Display --md-sys-typescale-display-md-size, -line-height, -weight
Headline --md-sys-typescale-headline-md-size, -line-height, -weight
Title --md-sys-typescale-title-md-size, -line-height, -weight
Body --md-sys-typescale-body-md-size, -line-height, -weight
Label --md-sys-typescale-label-md-size, -line-height, -weight
Emphasized --md-sys-typescale-emphasized-<role>-<size>

Language height. Line heights adapt to the script. Set --md-sys-language-height-scale (1, 1.07, 1.3, or 2) on :root to change the default; text in languages such as Arabic, Thai, or Urdu picks up its height from :lang().

Shape

Shape can direct attention, communicate state, and express brand.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/shape/

M3 Expressive uses a corner radius scale from straight to fully round, with larger steps, "increased" values, and shape morphing between states.

Tokens

Link to “Tokens” #

Tokens follow the naming convention --md-sys-shape-corner-<step>.

Shape Token
Corner --md-sys-shape-corner-none
  --md-sys-shape-corner-xs
  --md-sys-shape-corner-sm
  --md-sys-shape-corner-md
  --md-sys-shape-corner-lg, -lg-increased
  --md-sys-shape-corner-xl, -xl-increased
  --md-sys-shape-corner-xxl
  --md-sys-shape-corner-full

Steps also come in asymmetric variants (-xs-top, -lg-top, -lg-start, -lg-end, -xl-top) and as single values (--md-sys-shape-corner-value-<step>). Each step also has one token per corner, such as --md-sys-shape-corner-md-start-end, which defaults to the step's all-corner token; override one to shape a single corner.

--md-sys-shape-corner-full is 50cqmin (half the shorter side of the nearest size container), so it rounds fully only inside a container. Components that animate through "full" set it to half their own height.

Set data-shape-family="cut" on <html> to cut corners in browsers that support corner-shape.

Elevation

Elevation is the distance between two surfaces on the z-axis.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/elevation/

Elevation is the distance between two surfaces on the z-axis. It tells people which surface sits in front, which one sits behind, and which one is the current focus. Every surface and component has an elevation, so keep the number of levels small.

Levels

Link to “Levels” #

There are six levels, 0 to 5. Each one has a token:

  • --md-sys-elevation-shadow-0 (no shadow) to --md-sys-elevation-shadow-5

Levels 0 to 3 are for resting components. Levels 4 and 5 are for interaction states, such as hover and drag. Components raise by one level when hovered or focused: a FAB goes from level 3 to level 4, and a filled button goes from level 0 to level 1.

The tokens are defined in labs/gb/styles/elevation/md-elevation-tokens.scss. Shadow colors come from --md-sys-color-shadow, so they adapt to the color scheme.

Resting levels

Link to “Resting levels” #

Each component has a fixed resting level. Do not change it on your own.

Level Components
0 Buttons (filled, tonal, outlined), button group, split button, icon buttons, chips, segmented button, cards (filled, outlined), carousel, list, navigation rail, tabs, slider, app bar (not scrolled), full-screen dialog, docked side sheet
1 Elevated button, elevated card, elevated chip, modal navigation drawer, modal bottom sheet, modal side sheet
2 Menu, navigation bar, rich tooltip
3 FAB (small, standard and extended), FAB menu close button, modal dialog, date picker, time picker, floating toolbar, full-screen dialog above compact windows (where it is a basic dialog)

The search bar also rests at level 0 without a shadow, but it shows its level by tone (see below).

Showing elevation with tone

Link to “Showing elevation with tone” #

Elevation can be shown with a tonal surface color instead of a shadow. Two components do this in gb:

  • Search bar: no shadow. Its container uses surface-container-high, the tone for level 3.
  • App bar when scrolled: no drop shadow. Its container changes from surface to surface-container, the tone for level 2, so it separates from the content under it.

Use tone when a surface only needs to be told apart from what is behind it.

Shadows

Link to “Shadows” #

Shadows are for two cases only: to protect an element on a busy or patterned background, and to encourage interaction, such as a card that lifts on hover. Otherwise rely on the tonal difference between surfaces, which is the default. A small, sharp shadow means the surface is close to the one behind it. A larger, softer shadow means more distance.

Code sample

Link to “Code sample” #

What to watch out for

Link to “What to watch out for” #
  • Do not hard-code shadow values. Use the level tokens so a change to the scale reaches every surface.
  • Avoid changing the default elevation of a component. When an interaction such as hover changes it, make the change the same for every similar component.
  • Give floating elements enough contrast with the surface beneath them, either through the shadow or through a tone difference.

Icons

md-gb-icon shows a Material Symbols icon.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/icons/

md-gb-icon shows a Material Symbols icon. Its content is the ligature name of the symbol, such as home. Find names and previews at fonts.google.com/icons. Symbols come in three styles: outlined, rounded and sharp.

The element is a thin wrapper over the font. It reads its size, color and font variation settings from custom properties.

Loading the font

Link to “Loading the font” #

The element's default font family is Material Symbols. The Google Fonts family for the outlined style is Material Symbols Outlined, so set --md-icon-font to the family you load:

Load the font once in the page head. Request only the axes you use; add GRAD to use --md-icon-grad.

Size and color

Link to “Size and color” #
  • --md-icon-size sets the size. The default is 24px. Symbols support 20dp, 24dp, 40dp and 48dp; use 20dp for dense layouts and 40dp or 48dp for display use.
  • --md-icon-color sets the color. The default is currentColor.
  • The optical size follows the icon size automatically, so a larger icon gets a matching optical size. Set --md-icon-opsz only to override it.

Variable font axes

Link to “Variable font axes” #

Each style has four axes. The element exposes them as custom properties:

Property Axis Default Range Notes
--md-icon-wght Weight 400 100 to 700 400 is the 2dp stroke for standard icons. Use at least 200 at 24dp.
--md-icon-fill Fill 0 0 to 1 1 is filled, 0 is outlined. The change animates.
--md-icon-grad Grade 0 Negative to positive Gb sets -25 when the color scheme is dark, where icons are light on dark. Positive values add emphasis.
--md-icon-opsz Optical size follows size 20 to 48dp Not set by default.

Fill is the usual way to show a selected state. Use the outlined symbol when the item is unselected and the filled one when it is selected.

Baseline next to text

Link to “Baseline next to text” #

Symbols next to text need a baseline shift to line up. The element already applies vertical-align: -0.115em (of its own size), which lowers the icon so it lines up with the text beside it: about 2.8px at 24dp. Keep that vertical-align if you override the style, or the icon will look too high.

Targets

Link to “Targets” #

A 24dp icon needs a 48dp target by default. A 20dp icon can use a 40dp target when a mouse and keyboard are the main input. md-gb-icon-button keeps a 48dp minimum target (--target-size) even when the icon inside is smaller, so use it rather than a bare icon in a clickable element.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • An icon is decorative unless it has a label. md-gb-icon sets aria-hidden="true" by default, so screen readers skip it. That is correct when the text beside the icon already says what it means.
  • For an icon-only control, put the accessible name on the control with aria-label, and leave the icon hidden. Only set aria-hidden="false" on an icon that must be announced on its own.
  • Add a text label when the symbol is abstract, complex, or carries a key action. A symbol shown below 20dp should have one too.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Change an axis or the size with the custom properties.

Put the accessible name on the control, not on the icon.

What to watch out for

Link to “What to watch out for” #
  • An icon with no font loaded shows the ligature text, such as favorite, not a symbol. Load the font before the page relies on it.
  • Do not mix styles in one icon set. Pick outlined, rounded or sharp for the whole product.
  • Do not use the lightest weight for standard 24dp icons.
  • Keep the icon's content inside the 20dp live area of the 24dp grid. It can reach into the 2dp padding for extra weight, but never past the 24dp edge.

Material Symbols

md-gb-icon axes: optical size, weight, fill and grade.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/material-symbols/

Each variable font axis of md-gb-icon is a custom property. See Icons for loading the font and the defaults.

Optical sizes

Link to “Optical sizes” #

The optical size follows --md-icon-size, which supports 20, 24, 40 and 48px.

Weights

Link to “Weights” #

--md-icon-wght runs from 100 to 700.

Fill

Link to “Fill” #

--md-icon-fill is 0 (outlined) or 1 (filled), and the change animates.

Grades

Link to “Grades” #

--md-icon-grad adds emphasis when positive. It needs GRAD in the font request.

Motion

Motion makes a UI expressive and easy to follow: springs for physics, easing and duration tokens, and transition patterns.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/motion/

Overview

Link to “Overview” #

Material 3 Expressive uses a physics-based motion system. Springs drive spatial motion (position, size, rotation, corner shape) and effects springs drive properties that must not overshoot, like color and opacity. One spring can serve transitions, button effects and gestures, which keeps the product feeling consistent. Each spring is exposed as a CSS linear() easing with a matching duration, so a transition can use it directly.

Motion schemes

Link to “Motion schemes” #
  • Expressive is the default. Use it for most situations, especially hero moments and key interactions. Spatial springs overshoot and bounce into place.
  • Standard moves with minimal bounce and suits utilitarian products. Apply it to a subtree with the md-motion-standard class.

The spec's three levels of customization map to CSS like this:

  1. Use a default scheme: do nothing (Expressive), or add md-motion-standard.
  2. Create a custom scheme: override the spring custom properties in your own :root rule.
  3. Swap the scheme for one element: put md-motion-standard on that element.

Spring tokens

Link to “Spring tokens” #

Spring tokens follow --md-sys-motion-spring-<speed>-<spatial|effects>, with fast, default and slow speeds. Each has a -duration token:

Spring Expressive Standard
Spatial fast / default / slow 350 / 420 / 570ms 160 / 220 / 340ms
Effects fast / default / slow 140 / 220 / 300ms 140 / 220 / 300ms

Springs handle interruption and retargeting well, so prefer them. For animations without interruptions or gestures you can use the curve fallback: --md-sys-motion-curve-<speed>-<spatial|effects> (a cubic-bezier()) with --md-sys-motion-curve-<speed>-<spatial|effects>-duration. They carry the values from the spec's web conversion table.

Reduced motion

Link to “Reduced motion” #

Reduced motion is on when the platform asks for it (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) or inside an element with the md-motion-reduced class (spatial motion is off there, fades stay). The spatial springs then become instant (0ms) and the effects springs keep their timing. People still see fades and color changes, but not sliding, scaling, parallax or shape morphing.

Do not build your own motion gate. Read the durations from the tokens so the scheme and reduced motion apply without extra code.

Gestures

Link to “Gestures” #

A gesture has to keep its momentum: a fling that lets go at 2000px/s must not restart from rest, and a settle that is aimed at a new target half way must not jump. A CSS transition cannot do either, so labs/gb also has the same springs as physics, in labs/gb/components/shared/spring.ts. readSpring() returns the damping ratio and stiffness of a spring token (Expressive or Standard, whichever applies to the element), and Spring solves it in closed form and samples it every animation frame:

Under reduced motion the spring jumps to its target and rests at once. DragSettleController (the drag-and-settle behavior behind swipe to reveal, drawers, sheets and pane handles) does this for you when you pass onFrame: the settle starts at the release position with the release velocity, and the surface follows the frames with no CSS transition on the moved property. Without onFrame it keeps the CSS transition of the spring token.

Shape morphing

Link to “Shape morphing” #

Buttons and icon buttons (md-gb-button, md-gb-icon-button) morph their shape when pressed and when selected. That is spatial motion, so reduced motion turns it off and keeps the color change.

Component authors

Link to “Component authors” #

Components that script their motion use the helpers in labs/gb/components/shared/motion.ts:

  • springDuration(element, speed, kind) returns the duration of a spring in milliseconds, already 0 for spatial springs when motion is reduced.
  • isReducedMotion(element) and onReducedMotionChange(...) follow the setting, including inside .md-motion-reduced.
  • waitForMotion(...) resolves when the animations end or when its timeout runs out, so waiting never hangs. waitForDuration(ms, signal) is the plain timed wait.

Not covered

Link to “Not covered” #
  • The spec's Compose APIs (MotionScheme objects, a CompositionLocal per element) have no web equivalent. The CSS steps above replace them.
  • Springs are pre-sampled into linear() easings for transitions. A transition cannot take a starting velocity, so gestures use the solver described in Gestures instead.

Easing and duration

Link to “Easing and duration” #

M3 Expressive moves components to springs, but transitions still use the easing and duration system, and so can products that have not migrated yet. The spec offers a starting pair for each case:

Easing token Duration token Use it to
emphasized long2 (500ms) Begin and end on screen
emphasized-decelerate medium4 (400ms) Enter the screen
emphasized-accelerate short4 (200ms) Exit the screen
standard medium2 (300ms) Begin and end on screen, small utility transitions
standard-decelerate medium1 (250ms) Enter the screen
standard-accelerate short4 (200ms) Exit the screen

Tokens are --md-sys-motion-easing-<set>[-accelerate|-decelerate] and --md-sys-motion-duration-<short|medium|long|extra-long><1-4>. Short is 50 to 200ms, medium 250 to 400ms, long 450 to 600ms and extra long 700 to 1000ms, in steps of 50ms (extra long in steps of 100ms).

How to choose:

  • Easing set. Emphasized for most transitions, with its decelerate and accelerate variants for entering and exiting. Standard for small, quick, utility transitions.
  • Easing type. Plain for elements that begin and end on screen, decelerate when entering, accelerate when leaving for good. An element that leaves temporarily (a drawer that comes back) uses the plain curve.
  • Duration. Bigger transitions and larger distances take longer. Exits are shorter than enters, because the user's attention has already moved on.

Reduced motion does not change these tokens. Gate sliding and scaling yourself (the transition helpers below do) or use the spring tokens, which follow the setting.

Not covered: the spec's emphasized easing is a path curve. On the web --md-sys-motion-easing-emphasized is the single cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) approximation, so it is equal to standard.

Transitions

Link to “Transitions” #

A transition is a short animation that connects elements or full-screen views and shows how they relate. The spec defines six patterns and notes that they still use the easing and duration tokens above, not springs. labs/gb implements them in styles/motion/transitions/ with the View Transitions API, and falls back to the Web Animations API when the browser lacks it (or when you pass viewTransition: false).

The pattern styles are part of m3Styles (see Quick Start). Adopt them on the document, because ::view-transition-* rules only work there. The helpers come from @material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js.

Every helper takes update, a function that changes the DOM to the new state, and returns a promise that resolves when the motion ends. Common options: reducedMotion, viewTransition, duration and easing. The timings come from --md-transition-* custom properties (for example --md-transition-shared-axis-duration), so you can restyle a pattern in CSS.

Container transform

Link to “Container transform” #

For an element that becomes a new surface and shows more detail: a card that opens a details page, a FAB that opens a sheet, a search box, a list item. The container's bounds, corner radius and color morph while its content fades through (Emphasized, 500ms by default). from and to can be the same element or different ones. Swap them to collapse back.

Forward and backward

Link to “Forward and backward” #

For screens at consecutive levels of hierarchy, like an inbox and a message. The screens slide along the x axis as they fade (axis: 'y' and 'z' are available too). Always pair forward with backward when the user goes back, so the direction stays consistent.

scope limits the motion to one region. Without it the whole page animates.

Lateral

Link to “Lateral” #

For peers at the same level, like tabs or the photos in an album. Both pages slide the full width together. The direction is next or previous and follows the writing direction (RTL is handled).

Top level

Link to “Top level” #

For switching between top-level destinations (navigation bar, rail or drawer). The old screen quickly fades out, then the new one fades in, so they never overlap. These destinations are not related spatially, so there is no directional slide; the new screen only scales up slightly as it fades in.

Enter and exit

Link to “Enter and exit” #

For introducing or removing a component. enter(element, options) shows it (hidden = false) and exit(element, options) animates it away, then you hide or remove it. Both resolve when the animation ends.

  • Within screen bounds (menus, dialogs, snackbars, tooltips, FABs). The default style: 'expand' is the Android style: the component expands away from the nearest screen edge, without scale. style: 'scale' is the iOS style (scale in, fade out). Pick the edge with origin.
  • Beyond screen bounds (drawers, sheets, banners, navigation). style: 'slide' slides the component on and off from its edge. Set temporary: true for something that comes back, like a drawer, so it exits with the plain Emphasized curve instead of the accelerate one.

Match the origin to where the component lives: a notification from the top, a drawer from the start edge, a bottom sheet and the keyboard from the bottom. In templates, enterExitClasses(state, options) returns a classMap() object (md-transition-enter, md-transition-from-top and so on), and clearEnterExit(element) removes the classes.

Hide and reveal while scrolling

Link to “Hide and reveal while scrolling” #

A component can also leave and return based on a scroll gesture, to give more room for browsing: a top app bar or a navigation bar that slides off the screen edge while the user scrolls down and back on when they scroll up. scrollEnterExit(element, options) does this with the slide enter and exit motion and returns a handle with hidden, show(), hide() and destroy().

target is the scrolling element or its id (the window by default), origin the edge it slides toward. It uses the same scroll rules as the app bar and navigation bar, so they all behave alike: it reveals at the top and when scrolled up, hides after a short scroll down, never hides while focus is inside it, and reveals when focus moves into it. A hidden element is inert. With reduced motion it fades instead of sliding. Call destroy() when the element goes away. Components that already have scroll-behavior="hide" do not need this.

Coplanar components

Link to “Coplanar components” #

A coplanar component sits at the same elevation as the main content (a standard side sheet), so the content shrinks to make room as it enters and grows back as it exits. coplanar(element, open, options) animates the element's size from zero to its natural size with the enter motion (and back with the exit motion), so a flex or grid neighbor resizes with it. It shows the element when opening and sets hidden when closing ends.

axis: 'block' grows the element along the block axis instead of the inline axis. With reduced motion the size changes at once and only a fade plays. md-gb-side-sheet already does this itself: a standard (not modal) sheet takes its width as open is set, so the content beside it shrinks with its spring motion. Use coplanar() for your own panels.

Skeleton loaders

Link to “Skeleton loaders” #

For the step from a loading state to loaded content. The skeleton hints at where content will appear and holds its space, so the layout does not shift. It pulses subtly from the top left to the bottom right, and the content fades in on top when it is ready.

shape is rect, text or circle. While loading the element sets aria-busy="true" and makes its content inert. For markup without the element, use the classes md-skeleton, md-skeleton-text and md-skeleton-circle.

Accessibility and good practice

Link to “Accessibility and good practice” #

The spec asks transitions to follow accessibility settings, stay consistent, keep layouts stable, avoid jump cuts, use one spatial model and direction, fade cleanly and stay simple.

  • Every helper follows prefers-reduced-motion and replaces sliding and scaling with a quick fade. Pass reducedMotion: true to force it, as an app setting would.
  • Fade through never overlaps the old and new content. The content fade of a container transform is timed to the fastest part of the motion.
  • Use one pattern per kind of navigation, and keep forward and backward mirrored.
  • Dialogs and similar components that appear in place use the short fade (--md-transition-enter-fade-duration).

Watch out for

Link to “Watch out for” #
  • Keep most of a product on one scheme. Switch schemes only for a few key moments, and do it on purpose.
  • Do not use motion to carry meaning on its own. Reduced motion removes it, so pair it with a change people can see without motion.

Transitions

Transition patterns connect elements and views, and skeleton loaders hold space while content loads.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/motion-transitions/

The six transition patterns (container transform, forward and backward, lateral, top level, enter and exit, and skeleton loaders) are helper functions and classes. See Motion for the helpers.

Skeleton loaders

Link to “Skeleton loaders” #

A skeleton hints at where content will appear and holds its space while it loads. Set loading and clear it when the content is ready.

Spacing

Spacing is the distance around and between elements.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/spacing/

Spacing is the distance around and between elements. It shapes components (the space between an icon and its label) and layouts (the margin between the content and the window edge). Spacing follows an 8dp scale, and tokens keep that scale in one place.

Parts of spacing

Link to “Parts of spacing” #

There are three kinds:

  • Padding is the space inside an element, between its edge and its content.
  • Gaps are the spaces between elements in a row, column or grid.
  • Margins are the space outside an element, between it and its parent or the screen edge.

Each one can be vertical, horizontal, or on one edge: top, bottom, leading or trailing. Leading and trailing swap sides in right-to-left languages, so write them as logical properties (padding-inline, margin-inline-start).

Define padding and gaps on the parent container first. Margins on child elements are harder to keep uniform, so use them only for space beyond the parent's padding, or in a layout.

The scale

Link to “The scale” #

The unit is --md-sys-space-unit, 8px. Each token is a multiple of it. The token name is the value times 100, so space200 is 2 units (16px). The in-between values (2, 4, 6 and 10px) are nested units for small gaps, such as an icon and its label.

Token Value Token Value
--md-sys-space-0 0px --md-sys-space-400 32px
--md-sys-space-25 2px --md-sys-space-450 36px
--md-sys-space-50 4px --md-sys-space-500 40px
--md-sys-space-75 6px --md-sys-space-600 48px
--md-sys-space-100 8px --md-sys-space-700 56px
--md-sys-space-125 10px --md-sys-space-800 64px
--md-sys-space-150 12px --md-sys-space-900 72px
--md-sys-space-175 14px
--md-sys-space-200 16px
--md-sys-space-250 20px
--md-sys-space-300 24px

The tokens are defined in labs/gb/styles/space/md-space-tokens.scss. They are fixed pixel values, so they do not grow with the text size.

A product can add a token that follows the same pattern. For example, --md-sys-space-225: calc(var(--md-sys-space-unit) * 2.25) gives 18px.

Adaptive spacing

Link to “Adaptive spacing” #

Some spacing should change with the window. Three adaptive tokens do this:

  • --md-sys-space-adaptive-inline: horizontal padding
  • --md-sys-space-adaptive-block: vertical padding
  • --md-sys-space-adaptive-gap: gap between elements

Each one points at a scale token that depends on the window size class. The classes are the ones in Adaptive layout.

Class Inline Block Gap
compact 16px 16px 8px
medium 24px 24px 16px
expanded 24px 32px 16px
large 32px 32px 24px
extra-large 32px 40px 24px

Direct children of a .md-window element follow that element's width, so a layout can adapt to its pane rather than the screen. Other elements follow the viewport. The spacing unit does not change with the window.

The adaptive tokens are defined, but no labs/gb component reads them yet: component spacing is the same at every window size today. Use them in your own layouts, or remap a component's own spacing property to one (see below).

How components use spacing

Link to “How components use spacing” #

Components map their padding, margins and gaps to scale tokens in their own custom properties (--leading-space, --icon-label-space and so on), so a product can change one mapping and every use follows. For example, md-gb-button { --leading-space: var(--md-sys-space-adaptive-inline); } makes a button's leading padding follow the window class.

Component Scale tokens it reads
Button, icon button, FAB, split button, segmented button space50 to space200 for leading and trailing space and the icon-label gap
Search bar space0 to space300: leading space space200, icon and input gap space50, glyph margin space300 (24px), or space150 (12px) when focused. Styles are in labs/gb/components/search/
App bar space0 to space300 for icon, leading and trailing space, the title inset and bottom space, and the actions' inline margin
Toolbar, navigation drawer space50 to space200 for container padding and item spacing
Chip, text field, tooltip, menu, divider, badge, tabs space25 to space200 for padding, label gaps and insets
Date picker, time picker, carousel space50 to space900 for header, actions and content padding
App scaffold space200 for the FAB's distance from the edge and the gap above the bottom bar
Pane scaffold --md-sys-layout-margin and --md-sys-layout-spacer (the layout tokens), not the scale

Every value is the same as before, so nothing changes visually. A few values are still plain pixels: some generated button, list, FAB, button group and navigation rail values, the dialog and sheet paddings, and the few values a component reads in code (a carousel's leading padding, a tooltip's viewport margin, a tab indicator's inset).

Density changes components, not the spacing scale. Each density step removes height from the component, and the component's touch target stays 48dp. See Density.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #

The spec's accessibility guidance is one point: when text is scaled up to 200%, keep the same spacing. Spacing tokens are fixed in pixels, so the spacing stays the same while the text grows. For touch targets and focus, see Accessibility.

What to watch out for

Link to “What to watch out for” #
  • Use the scale tokens, not hardcoded pixel values. A raw 16px will not follow a remapped token.
  • Set spacing on the parent, not the children, unless you need space beyond the parent's padding.
  • Use logical properties (padding-inline, gap) so right-to-left layouts flip correctly.
  • Do not adapt spacing to density yourself. Set the density attribute on the component and let it apply its own steps.
  • Keep the spacing the same at 200% text. Do not replace a token with a value that grows with the text.

Button Group

A button group arranges related buttons and can manage their selection, density and overflow.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/button-group/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-button-group.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Choose standard or connected. In a standard group, buttons respond to the one that is pressed; a connected group joins them into one control.
  • Keep buttons alike. Use the same size and shape for every button, and mix sizes only for hero moments.
  • Group related buttons. Mix colors and widths to emphasize what matters and to group related actions.
  • Let it adapt. On narrow screens, trailing buttons can collapse into an overflow menu.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A button group holds md-gb-button elements, each with an optional icon.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Connected

Link to “Connected” #

Set variant="connected" for buttons that sit together as a single control.

Selection

Link to “Selection” #

Set selection to single or multiple and give each button a value. Add required to keep one selected in a single-select group. A group fires input and change when selection changes.

Icons

Link to “Icons” #

Buttons in a group can be icon-only. Give each one an aria-label.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) to -3 to make the buttons shorter. Touch targets stay 48px.

Overflow menu

Link to “Overflow menu” #

Add overflow-menu to collapse the buttons that don't fit into a menu at the trailing edge. Choosing a menu entry clicks the original button.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The group does not need a label of its own, but a name such as aria-label="Text alignment" helps when the buttons form a set.
  • Label each button as you would a button; icon-only buttons need aria-label.
  • Tab enters the group, Arrow keys move between buttons, and Enter or Space activates the focused button.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

API reference

Link to “API reference” #

<md-gb-button-group>

Link to “<md-gb-button-group>” #

A Material Design button group.

Properties

Link to “Properties” #
Property Attribute Type Default
density
The density of the buttons inside, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the buttons' height (button-groups.md: "Button groups adapt to the height of the buttons inside, including when density is applied"); touch targets stay 48px. A button's own non-zero density wins. Values are clamped to that range.		 density Density
disabled
Whether the button group is disabled.		 disabled boolean false
overflowMenu
Whether the buttons at the trailing edge that do not fit collapse into a trailing overflow menu, and come back when the group has room again (button-groups.md, Adaptive design: "Buttons at the trailing edge of the button group can be customized to collapse into an overflow menu at smaller breakpoints, and become visible again at larger sizes."). The group is as wide as its container allows: give it a width, or put it in a narrower container, to make buttons overflow. Choosing a menu entry clicks the original button.		 overflow-menu boolean false
required
Whether selection is required in single-select mode.		 required boolean false
resizing
How the group and its buttons resize (button-groups.md, Resizing). fixed: every button keeps the width its own size and width give it. flexible: the group fills the width of its container and its buttons grow with it; an icon button does not stretch past its set width, and a button with resizing="fixed" keeps its width. A button with resizing="flexible" in a fixed group grows when the group is given more width. Unset: a connected group is flexible (it spans its surface), a standard group is fixed.		 resizing ButtonGroupResizing ""
selection
The selection mode.		 selection ButtonGroupSelection "none"

Buttons

Buttons help people initiate actions, from sending an email, to sharing a document, to liking a post.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/button/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-button.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Label the action. A button's text describes what happens when it is pressed, such as "Save" or "Join now".
  • Match emphasis to importance. Use filled for the final action of a flow, tonal and outlined for medium emphasis, and text for the lowest priority.
  • Use elevated sparingly. Elevated buttons add a shadow, so reserve them for buttons that need separation from a patterned background.
  • Add an icon to draw attention. An icon can help communicate the action.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A button is one element holding a label and an optional icon (default slot). It renders a native <button> or, with href, a link.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Choose one of five colors with the color attribute: filled, elevated, tonal, outlined, or text.

Sizes

Link to “Sizes” #

Set size to xs, sm (default), md, lg, or xl.

With an icon

Link to “With an icon” #

Put an md-gb-icon before the label, or after it for an action that leaves the page.

Square shape

Link to “Square shape” #

Add square to change the shape of the button from round to square.

Toggle

Link to “Toggle” #

Set type="toggle" to make a button that stays selected after it is pressed. Add selected for the initial state.

Disabled and soft-disabled

Link to “Disabled and soft-disabled” #

A disabled button can't be focused with the keyboard. A soft-disabled button stays focusable, which helps discoverability in toolbars.

Opening a popover or menu

Link to “Opening a popover or menu” #

Like a native button, an md-gb-button (and md-gb-icon-button) takes popovertarget (with popovertargetaction) or commandfor (with command) naming an element in the same tree. A menu opened this way also opens with the arrow keys.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Buttons need a visible label; add an aria-label to icon-only buttons or when the label needs to be more descriptive.
  • Buttons activate with Enter and Space and are reachable with Tab.
  • Disabled buttons leave the tab order. Use soft-disabled to keep one focusable, as the ARIA guidance on disabled controls allows.
  • Toggle buttons expose their state with aria-pressed.

FAB menu

A FAB menu opens from a FAB to show several related actions, and the FAB becomes its close button.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/fab-menu/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-fab-menu.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Open it from a FAB. The menu appears where the FAB was, and not from an extended FAB or any other component.
  • Keep it related. A menu holds 2 to 6 closely related actions under one purpose, such as sharing.
  • Align to the trailing edge. The FAB and menu sit at the trailing edge of the window, mirrored in right-to-left languages.
  • Always label items. Every item needs a text label.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A FAB menu holds items and a FAB that toggles it. Both icons can be replaced.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Set color to primary (default), secondary or tertiary.

Size

Link to “Size” #

Set size to md or lg for a larger FAB.

Start alignment

Link to “Start alignment” #

Set align="start" to align the items to the start edge, as for a FAB at the leading side.

Open and events

Link to “Open and events” #

Set open to open the menu from code. The toggle event fires before it opens or closes and activate fires before an item closes it; cancel either to keep the menu as it is.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Name the menu with aria-label, such as "Message actions". It labels the toggle button.
  • The toggle button exposes whether the menu is expanded or collapsed.
  • Tab moves through the button and the items, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
  • A menu over scrolling content shouldn't hide focused elements. Register it with setupScrollPadding() from appbar/scroll-padding.js.

Floating action button (FAB)

A FAB represents the most important action on a screen, and an extended FAB adds a text label.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/fab/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-fab.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • One main action. Use a FAB for the most important action on a screen. It floats in front of other content.
  • Pick a size. Choose by visual hierarchy: the default FAB, a medium FAB (most recommended) or a large FAB.
  • Add a label for emphasis. An extended FAB shows a text label next to its icon. It can collapse while a page scrolls.
  • Place it consistently. A FAB can sit at the start, center or end, above a navigation bar or nested in it.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A FAB holds an icon in its default slot. Set label to make it an extended FAB.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Extended

Link to “Extended” #

Set label for an extended FAB. The label is its accessible name.

Without an icon

Link to “Without an icon” #

An extended FAB is the only FAB that can leave out its icon.

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Set color to primary, primary-container (default), secondary, secondary-container, tertiary or tertiary-container.

Sizes

Link to “Sizes” #

Set size to md or lg. The default is the standard FAB. sm is a 40dp FAB that the spec no longer recommends.

Collapsed

Link to “Collapsed” #

Set expanded="false" to collapse an extended FAB to an icon-only FAB. Set the expanded property to change it later.

Collapse on scroll

Link to “Collapse on scroll” #

Set scroll-target to the id of a scrolling container, or window. The FAB collapses while it scrolls down and expands while it scrolls up. A cancelable toggle event fires first.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • An icon-only FAB needs an aria-label that describes its action, such as "Compose a new message".
  • An extended FAB uses its label as its name, also while collapsed. Add aria-label only for more context.
  • An icon-only FAB shows a tooltip on hover and focus. Set tooltip="false" to turn it off.
  • A FAB fixed over scrolling content shouldn't hide focused elements. Register it with setupScrollPadding() from appbar/scroll-padding.js.
  • Tab focuses the FAB, and Enter or Space activates it.

Link to “Compatibility” #

Icon Buttons

Icon buttons help people take supplementary actions with a single tap.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/icon-button/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-icon-button.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use a clear icon. Pick a system icon whose meaning people already know, and give the button an accessible name that describes the action.
  • Describe the action on hover. On the web, add a tooltip so the action is named while hovering or focusing the button.
  • Pick the color by emphasis. Filled is the most prominent, tonal and outlined are medium, and the standard color suits the lowest priority.
  • Show state with a toggle. A toggle button uses the outlined icon when unselected and the filled icon when selected.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

An icon button is one element that holds an icon (default slot). It renders a native <button> or, with href, a link.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Choose one of four colors with the color attribute: filled, tonal, outlined, or standard (the default).

Sizes

Link to “Sizes” #

Set size to xs, sm (default), md, lg, or xl.

Widths

Link to “Widths” #

Set width to narrow or wide. The default width sits in between.

Square shape

Link to “Square shape” #

Add square to change the shape of the button from round to square.

Toggle

Link to “Toggle” #

Set type="toggle" to make a button that stays selected after it is pressed. Add selected for the initial state. The selected button shows the filled icon; if an icon has no filled version, add unfilled-icon and it gets a heavier weight instead.

Tooltip

Link to “Tooltip” #

Add tooltip to show the button's aria-label on hover and keyboard focus. Write the label as the action, not the icon's name.

Links

Link to “Links” #

Set href to render the button as a link. Use target and rel as you would on an anchor.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) down to -3 to remove 4px of height per step. The touch target stays at least 48px. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

Disabled and soft-disabled

Link to “Disabled and soft-disabled” #

A disabled button can't be focused with the keyboard. A soft-disabled button stays focusable, which helps discoverability in toolbars.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • An icon button has no visible text, so always give it an aria-label that describes the action.
  • Icon buttons activate with Enter and Space and are reachable with Tab.
  • Disabled buttons leave the tab order. Use soft-disabled to keep one focusable, as the ARIA guidance on disabled controls allows.
  • Toggle buttons expose their state with aria-pressed.

A segmented button set lets people pick one or several options from two to five segments, such as a time range or a view.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/segmented-button/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-segmented-button.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Prefer a connected button group. Material 3 Expressive no longer recommends segmented buttons; the connected button group has mostly the same function with an updated look.
  • Keep it to two to five segments. For more options or more complex choices, use chips.
  • Pick the selection mode. A set is single-select by default; add multiselect when people can choose several.
  • Use icons, labels or both. Make sure each icon-only segment has an accessible name.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A segmented button set holds segments. Each segment has a label and an optional icon.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Multi-select

Link to “Multi-select” #

Add multiselect to the set so people can select more than one segment. A selected segment shows a checkmark; add no-checkmark to a segment to hide it.

Icons

Link to “Icons” #

Put an md-gb-icon in the icon slot, with or without a label. An icon-only segment needs an aria-label.

Required

Link to “Required” #

In a single-select set, add required so a segment always stays selected and the selected one can't be unselected.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

Add disabled to a segment, or to the set to disable every segment.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density on the set from 0 (default, 40px tall) down to -3 to remove 4px of height per step. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

In a form

Link to “In a form” #

The set is form-associated. Give it a name and it submits the selected segment's value, one entry for each selected segment in a multi-select set. It fires input and change when people change the selection.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Give the set an aria-label that says what the choice is about.
  • In a single-select set the segments are radios, and in a multi-select set they are checkboxes. Tab enters the set, the arrow keys move between segments, and Space or Enter selects the focused one.
  • Icon-only segments need an aria-label.
  • A disabled segment is skipped by the keyboard.

Split button

A split button pairs a main action with a trailing button that opens a menu of related actions.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/split-button/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-split-button.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • One main action plus related ones. The leading button runs the most common action, and the menu holds the alternatives.
  • Same sizes as buttons. Split buttons come in the five button sizes, so they can sit next to buttons and icon buttons of the same size.
  • Trailing menu icon. The trailing button always shows the menu icon. Its color doesn't change when the menu opens; it only turns.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A split button holds a leading button, a trailing button and the menu the trailing button opens.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Split buttons are filled by default. Set color to elevated, tonal or outlined.

Sizes

Link to “Sizes” #

Set size to xs, sm (the default), md, lg or xl.

Leading icon

Link to “Leading icon” #

The leading button can have an icon, a label, or both.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Both parts are native <button>s you provide, so give the trailing button an aria-label that says what the menu holds, such as "More save options". Add one to an icon-only leading button too.
  • The two buttons are separate tab stops. The trailing button toggles the menu with popovertarget, and the menu follows the menu keyboard behavior.

Date picker

A date picker lets people select a date or a range of dates.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/date-picker/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-date-picker.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Match the context. Use the docked picker, a calendar under a text field, on medium and expanded windows. Use a modal picker on compact ones.
  • Pick or type. A modal picker has a calendar mode and an input mode for typing a date.
  • Select a range. Add range to choose a start and an end date.
  • Offer a way to clear. Add clearable so people can remove a selection.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A date picker is one element. A docked picker renders a text field and a calendar popup; a modal picker renders a dialog.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Modal

Link to “Modal” #

Set variant="modal" and call show() to open the picker in a dialog. Use mode="input" to start with the date input.

Range

Link to “Range” #

Add range to select a start and an end date. The value is an ISO interval such as 2026-08-17/2026-08-23.

Value, min and max

Link to “Value, min and max” #

Set value to an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Limit the choices with min and max.

Full screen

Link to “Full screen” #

Add fullscreen to a modal picker for compact windows. It has a close button and a Save button.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Name the field with label, such as "Event date", and use supporting-text to show the expected format.
  • Calendar targets stay 48px, so density only affects the text fields.
  • Page Up and Page Down move by month, and Shift with them moves by year.
  • The modal picker closes with Escape, and the docked picker confirms with Enter.

<md-gb-date-picker>

Link to “<md-gb-date-picker>” #

A Material Design date picker (docked or modal, single date or range).

Properties

Link to “Properties” #
Property Attribute Type Default
clearable
Shows a Clear button that removes the selection.		 clearable boolean false
density
The density of the picker's text fields (the docked field and the modal input mode's fields), from 0 (default) to -3, as md-gb-text-field density. Values are clamped to that range. The calendar itself never gets denser (date-pickers.md, Accessibility: "Interactive targets for all elements meet Material's 48x48dp minimum touch target requirement. Increasing density would negatively impact accessibility by limiting tappable/clickable targets"): its dates, menus and buttons keep their size, including inside a dense container.		 density Density
error
Forces the error state of the docked field.		 error boolean false
errorText
The message shown on the docked field while error is set.		 error-text string ''
firstDayOfWeek
The first day of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday). -1 (default) uses the locale's.		 first-day-of-week number -1
fullscreen
Modal: the full-screen layout the spec recommends on compact windows. The dialog covers the window and has a close (x) icon button and a Save button in place of Cancel and OK.		 fullscreen boolean false
hideActions
Hides the Cancel and OK buttons; a selection is committed right away.		 hide-actions boolean false
inline
Renders the calendar surface in the page flow, always visible, instead of a docked popup (without the text field) or a modal dialog.		 inline boolean false
isDateDisabled
Returns true for dates that can't be selected (in addition to dates outside min / max). Receives an ISO date.		 (date: string) => boolean null
label
Docked: the text field label. Defaults to "Date" (range: "Dates").		 label string ''
locale
A BCP 47 locale. Defaults to the document's lang, else the browser's.		 locale string ''
max
The latest selectable date (ISO).		 max string ''
min
The earliest selectable date (ISO).		 min string ''
mode
Modal: shows the calendar (picker) or the date input (input).		 mode DatePickerMode 'picker'
open
Whether the popup (docked) or dialog (modal) is open.		 open boolean
quick
Skips animations.		 quick boolean false
range
Selects a start and end date.		 range boolean false
required
A value is required: with no date (or a range without an end date) the picker is invalid (valueMissing).		 required boolean false
strings
Overrides for the user-facing strings.		 Partial<DatePickerStrings> {}
supportingText
Docked: the field's supporting text. Defaults to the date format, e.g. MM/DD/YYYY.		 supporting-text string ''
value
The committed value: an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), or an ISO interval (start/end) when range is set. Empty when nothing is selected.		 value string ''
variant
docked (default) or modal.		 variant DatePickerVariant 'docked'

Events

Link to “Events” #
Event Description
cancel
Event		 The selection was dismissed (Cancel, Escape or a click outside). Cancelable: canceling keeps the picker open.
change
CustomEvent<DatePickerValueDetail>		 The value was committed (OK, Enter, typing in the docked field, or a pick with hide-actions).
close
CustomEvent<{reason: string}>		 The popup or dialog began closing; reason is confirm or cancel.
input
CustomEvent<DatePickerValueDetail>		 The pending selection changed (a date was picked or a valid date typed).
open
Event		 The popup or dialog opened.

Methods

Link to “Methods” #
Method Description
cancel
(reason?: string) => boolean		 Discards the pending selection: fires a cancelable cancel event, then closes the popup or dialog.
close
(reason?: string) => Promise<void>		 Closes the popup or dialog without changing the value (use confirm() to commit the pending selection).
confirm
() => boolean		 Commits the pending selection to value (firing change if it changed) and closes the popup or dialog. In the date input mode, invalid text shows its error and keeps the picker open.
focus
(options?: FocusOptions) => void		 MDN Reference
show
() => Promise<void>		 Opens the calendar popup (docked) or dialog (modal). The pending selection starts from value, and focus moves to the selected date (or today).
showMonth
(year: number, month: number) => void		 Shows the given month (year, month 1-12) in the calendar.

Time picker

Time pickers let people choose an hour and minute on a clock dial, or type them into fields.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/time-picker/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-time-picker.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Dial or input. The dial is quick for picking an approximate time, and typing is faster for an exact one. People can switch between them unless you hide the toggle.
  • Inline or modal. Show the picker inline in a form, or as a modal when it opens from a field or button.
  • Match the locale. The picker follows the 12 or 24 hour clock of its locale. Set hour-cycle to force one.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A time picker has a headline, the hour and minute selectors, an AM or PM toggle in 12 hour mode, a dial, and the actions.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Inline and modal

Link to “Inline and modal” #

Add modal to show the picker in a dialog with a scrim. Open it with show(). It fires change when a time is confirmed and cancel when it is dismissed.

Input mode

Link to “Input mode” #

Set mode="input" to start with hour and minute fields instead of the dial. Add hide-mode-toggle to remove the switch between the two.

Hour cycle

Link to “Hour cycle” #

Set hour-cycle to 12 or 24. The value is always a 24 hour HH:MM string.

Orientation

Link to “Orientation” #

The dial sits below the time selectors (vertical), except in short landscape windows, where it moves beside them (horizontal). Set orientation to choose one.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) to -3 to make the picker more compact.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Input mode is an alternative to the dial, and every control has a label. Localize the labels with attributes such as select-hour-label, hour-label, cancel-label and confirm-label.
  • A modal picker is a <dialog>: focus moves into it and returns to the opener on close, and Escape cancels.
  • In the dial, the arrow keys change the selected hour or minute.

The density, from 0 (default) to -3 (time-pickers.md "Density", "High-density time picker"). Each step down removes 4px from the time selectors (80px), input fields (72px), the period selector (which follows their height) and the dial (256px); the time selectors, fields and dial labels stay at least 48px. The horizontal layout, used when the viewport is short, keeps the full-size dial ("Don't apply density to the time picker dial when the viewport is constrained. Instead, use an input picker"). Values are clamped to that range.		 density Density

Accessible label of the mode toggle in input mode.		 dial-mode-label string 'Switch to clock mode'

The headline. Defaults to "Select time" (dial) or "Enter time" (input).		 headline string ''
hideActions
Hides the Cancel and OK actions; every change commits the value.		 hide-actions boolean false
hideModeToggle
Hides the dial / input mode toggle button.		 hide-mode-toggle boolean false
hourCycle
12 (with an AM/PM period selector), 24, or '' (default) to follow the locale's clock (Intl.DateTimeFormat).		 hour-cycle TimePickerHourCycle ''
hourLabel
Hour field label (input mode).		 hour-label string 'Hour'
inputModeLabel

locale
The locale used for the 12/24-hour default and the AM/PM labels. Defaults to the browser locale.		 locale string ''
minuteLabel
Minute field label (input mode).		 minute-label string 'Minute'
modal
Renders the picker as a modal dialog, shown with show() or open.		 modal boolean false
mode
dial (clock dial) or input (hour and minute text fields).		 mode TimePickerMode 'dial'
open
Whether a modal picker is open. Setting it opens or closes the picker.		 open boolean
orientation
The dial layout: vertical, horizontal, or '' (default) to pick one from the viewport (horizontal in short landscape viewports).		 orientation "" TimePickerOrientation
periodLabel
Accessible label of the period selector.		 period-label string 'Select AM or PM'
quick
Skips transitions.		 quick boolean false
required
Whether a time is required: with no time the picker is invalid (valueMissing) and blocks the form's submit.		 required boolean false
selectHourLabel
Accessible label of the hour selector and the dial in hour mode.		 select-hour-label string 'Select hour'
selection
Which part of the time the dial edits.		 TimePickerSelection 'hour'
selectMinuteLabel
Accessible label of the minute selector and the dial in minute mode.		 select-minute-label string 'Select minutes'
value
The committed time as a 24-hour HH:MM string (<input type="time"> format), or '' when no time is set.		 value string

Events

Link to “Events” #
Event Description
cancel
Event		 Fired when picking is canceled (Cancel, Escape, scrim click). Cancelable for a modal picker; canceling keeps it open.
change
Event		 Fired when a new value is committed (OK, or the end of an interaction with hide-actions).
close
Event		 Fired when a modal picker closes.
input
Event		 Fired whenever the picked time changes (dial drag, key, typed digits, period). Read the pending time from pendingValue.
open
Event		 Fired when a modal picker opens.

Methods

Link to “Methods” #
Method Description
cancel
(reason?: string) => void		 Discards the pending time and fires cancel; a modal picker closes unless the event is canceled (canceling keeps the pending time). What the Cancel action does.
close
(reason?: string) => Promise<void>		 Closes a modal picker without committing. Fires a cancelable close event with detail.reason, then closed after the exit transition.
confirm
() => void		 Commits the pending time to value (firing change when it differs) and closes a modal picker. What the OK action does.
show
() => Promise<void>		 Opens a modal picker on the committed time, starting with the hours. Fires open.
toggleMode
() => void		 Switches between the dial and input modes.

Loading indicator

A loading indicator shows that a short process is running, with a shape that morphs through Material shapes while it turns.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/loading-indicator/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-loading-indicator.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it for short waits. A loading indicator suits processes that finish in under five seconds, and replaces most uses of an indeterminate circular progress indicator.
  • Reflect real work. It always represents an ongoing process and is never only decorative.
  • Don't switch to determinate. Avoid it for processes that start indeterminate and later report progress; use a progress indicator there.
  • Use it for refreshing. A pull to refresh container shows a contained loading indicator.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A loading indicator is one element: a shape, with an optional container behind it.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Contained

Link to “Contained” #

Add contained to put the shape on a container, which helps it stand out over content.

Determinate

Link to “Determinate” #

Set value from 0 to 1 to show progress. Without it, the indicator is indeterminate.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The indicator is a progressbar, so give it an aria-label that says what is loading.
  • A determinate indicator exposes its value to assistive technology.
  • With reduced motion, the shape stops morphing and only turns slowly.

Progress indicators

Progress indicators inform people about the status of ongoing processes, such as loading an app or submitting a form.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/progress/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-progress.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Pick the variant. Use linear for progress across a page or container and circular for a compact spot such as a button or a card.
  • Use the same style for the same process. Keep one configuration for all the instances of a process, like loading.
  • Show real progress when you know it. Set a value for determinate progress, and leave it off when the length of the process is unknown.
  • Use wavy sparingly. A wavy active indicator is more expressive; use it where that fits your product.
  • For short waits, use a loading indicator. The loading indicator replaces most indeterminate circular progress indicators.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A progress indicator is one element: an active indicator over a track. It is linear unless circular is set.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Linear

Link to “Linear” #

The default indicator animates along a horizontal track.

Circular

Link to “Circular” #

Add circular to animate clockwise along a circular track.

Determinate

Link to “Determinate” #

Set value from 0 to 1 when you know how far along the process is. Without a value, the indicator is indeterminate.

Wavy

Link to “Wavy” #

Add wavy to give the active indicator a wave. It works on linear and circular indicators, determinate or not.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A progress indicator is a progressbar. Give it an aria-label that says what is in progress, such as "Download progress".
  • A determinate indicator exposes its value from 0 to 100 to assistive technology. An indeterminate one has no value.

Pull to refresh

A pull to refresh container lets people pull its content down to reload it, with a loading indicator that shows progress.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/pull-to-refresh/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-pull-to-refresh.json (setup)

Pull to refresh is the pull-to-refresh behavior of the loading indicator, which it shows while the content reloads.

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Refresh content people expect to change. Use it on feeds and lists that update, such as news or messages.
  • Always offer another way. Pulling isn't available to everyone, so provide a refresh button that people can use with a single pointer or the keyboard.
  • Show it is working. The container keeps the indicator in view until you set refreshing back to false.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A pull to refresh container holds the scrolling content (default slot). An indicator appears above it while people pull and while it refreshes.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Refresh button

Link to “Refresh button” #

Call refresh() from a button to start the same refresh without a gesture. It fires refresh and sets refreshing.

Circular indicator

Link to “Circular indicator” #

Set indicator="circular" to use a circular arrow and progress indicator instead of the default contained loading indicator.

Threshold and disabled

Link to “Threshold and disabled” #

Set threshold to the distance in pixels people must pull before releasing starts a refresh (the default is 80). Add disabled to turn pulling off.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Pulling needs a drag, so also provide a button or another control that calls refresh(), usable with a single pointer or the keyboard.
  • While refreshing, the indicator is a progressbar named by indicator-label (the default is "Refreshing"), and the label is announced politely. Write a label that says what is refreshing, such as "Refreshing news".

Navigation Bar

A navigation bar lets people switch between a small number of top-level destinations, and can hide as the page scrolls.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/navigation-bar/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-nav-bar.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it in compact and medium windows. From expanded windows up, switch to a navigation rail.
  • Keep three to five destinations. They should be of equal importance.
  • Keep destinations consistent. The same destinations appear on every screen of the app.
  • Pick the item layout. Use vertical items in compact windows and horizontal items from medium windows.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A navigation bar holds items. Each item has an icon, a label and an optional badge.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Item layout

Link to “Item layout” #

Set item-layout to vertical (the default) or horizontal. With auto, items are vertical in compact windows and horizontal from 600px.

Badges

Link to “Badges” #

Set badge on an item to show a count, or badge="dot" for a small dot that signals something new.

Links

Link to “Links” #

Give an item an href (and optionally target and rel) to make the destination a link, as in the first example. The item then has the link role and the selected one is marked aria-current="page". Without href an item is a tab that just reports the selection.

Hide on scroll

Link to “Hide on scroll” #

Set scroll-behavior="hide" to hide the bar when the page scrolls down and show it again on scroll up. By default it follows the window; set scroll-target to the id of another scrolling element. Fix the bar to the bottom of the page.

Selection

Link to “Selection” #

The active item shows the current destination, and selected-index selects an item by position. The bar fires change when the selection changes.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Give the bar an aria-label such as "Primary navigation".
  • Without links the bar is a tab list and its items are tabs, with exactly one selected. Tab moves focus into the bar, the arrow keys move between items, and Enter and Space select one.
  • When the items have an href the bar is a navigation landmark of links and the selected one is aria-current="page". Enter follows a link; Space doesn't.
  • Every item needs a visible label, which is also its accessible name. If the label is ambiguous, add a more descriptive aria-label to the item.
  • A hidden bar never hides while focus is inside it or when the page scrolls from a key press, and it reappears when focus moves into it. Leave scroll-behavior off if screen reader users rely on the bar.
  • Disabled items leave the tab order.
