Navigation Drawer

A Material Design navigation drawer.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/navigation-drawer/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-nav-drawer.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it for top-level destinations. A drawer lists the main sections of an app, with the current one selected.
  • Choose standard or modal. A standard drawer (above) sits beside the content on large windows; a modal drawer opens over a scrim on small ones.
  • Group with labels. Use section labels and dividers to organize long lists.
  • Keep labels short. Long labels truncate.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A drawer holds an optional headline, section labels, dividers, and items.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Modal drawer

Link to “Modal drawer” #

Set modal to open the drawer over a scrim. Escape, the scrim, or swiping closes it.

Modal drawer without swipe

Link to “Modal drawer without swipe” #

Set gestures-disabled on a modal drawer to turn off swipe-to-close. Escape, the scrim, and close() still work.

Text labels only

Link to “Text labels only” #

Items work without icons. Labels that are too long truncate, and disabled items are not interactive.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The drawer renders a <nav> landmark; give it a name with aria-label.
  • The selected item is the current page and is exposed with aria-current.
  • A modal drawer is a dialog: it traps focus, closes with Escape, and returns focus to what opened it.
  • Tab moves through the items; Enter activates a link item.

Navigation Rail

A navigation rail lets people switch between top-level destinations on larger windows, and expands to show full labels.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/navigation-rail/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-nav-rail.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it in medium windows and larger. On compact windows use a navigation bar instead.
  • Keep three to seven destinations. Add an optional FAB or menu button in the header.
  • Keep it in the same place. The rail stays at the leading edge on every screen of the app.
  • Let it expand. A collapsed rail shows icons and short labels, and an expanded rail shows horizontal items and can replace a navigation drawer.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A rail has an optional header, such as a menu button or a FAB, and items. Each item has an icon, a label and an optional badge.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Links

Link to “Links” #

Give an item an href (and optionally target and rel) to make the destination a link, as in the first example. The item then has the link role and the selected one is marked aria-current="page". Without href an item is a tab that just reports the selection.

Collapsible

Link to “Collapsible” #

Add collapsible to show a built-in menu button in the header that expands and collapses the rail. To use your own button, put it in the header slot and call toggle(), expand() or collapse(). Set expanded to start expanded. The rail fires toggle when it expands or collapses.

Header

Link to “Header” #

Use the header slot for a menu button and a FAB above the items.

Alignment

Link to “Alignment” #

Set alignment to top (the default), center or bottom to place the items along the rail.

Badges

Link to “Badges” #

Set badge on an item to show a count, or badge="dot" for a small dot.

Secondary items

Link to “Secondary items” #

Add secondary to an item that should show only while the rail is expanded, such as a less important destination.

Modal

Link to “Modal” #

Add modal so the expanded rail opens over the content with a scrim. Add hide-when-collapsed to take the collapsed rail out of the layout entirely; the app's menu button then calls toggle() to show it. On Android, the back gesture collapses a modal rail.

Appearance

Link to “Appearance” #

Add divider to draw a line at the rail's edge, elevated to lift it above scrolling content, and narrow to use the 80dp collapsed width.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Give the rail an aria-label such as "Primary navigation".
  • Without links the rail is a tab list and its items are tabs, with exactly one selected. Tab moves focus into the rail, the arrow keys move between items, and Enter and Space select one.
  • When the items have an href the rail is a navigation landmark of links and the selected one is aria-current="page". Enter follows a link; Space doesn't.
  • Every item needs a visible label, which is also its accessible name.
  • Give a menu button in the header an aria-label, such as "Open menu".
  • A modal rail collapses on Escape and when the scrim is pressed. Keep the menu button available as the single-pointer alternative to swiping it closed.
  • Disabled items leave the tab order.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

134 of 311 buildable spec units are tested, 11 are excluded with a written reason and 0 are uncovered (the target is 0). 46 of 92 token declarations match the spec (50%), and 46 have no spec token.

collapse

handleBack
() => Promise<void>		 Handles a back request (the Android back gesture or button) on the modal expanded rail: plays the predictive back motion, then collapses the rail. Call it for an in-app back control that should behave like the system back. Resolves after the back motion.

CSS parts

Link to “CSS parts” #
Part Description
::part(header) The navigation rail's header container.
::part(items) The navigation rail's items container.
::part(menu-button) The built-in expand/collapse menu button when collapsible.
::part(nav-rail) The navigation rail's root container.
::part(scrim) The modal rail's scrim, while expanded. A modal rail expands over the content with a scrim, like Compose ModalWideNavigationRail. Clicking the scrim, pressing Escape or swiping the rail toward its edge collapses it. The scrim (and the menu button of a collapsible rail) are the single-pointer alternatives to the swipe. While a modal rail is expanded, focus moves into it, Tab stays inside it, page scrolling is locked, and focus returns to the previous element when it collapses. The toggle event's detail.reason says why a modal rail collapsed (escape, back, scrim or swipe). Predictive back applies to the modal expanded rail (navigation-rail.md): while it is expanded the rail listens for back requests with a CloseWatcher (the Android back gesture or button, and Escape), falling back to Escape on the document where CloseWatcher is missing. A back request plays the predictive back motion (the rail pops off its edge, Compose ModalWideNavigationRail scales) and collapses the rail. A FAB (md-gb-fab with a label) in the header is an extended FAB while the rail is expanded and an icon FAB while it is collapsed.

Sheets

Sheets show supplementary content and actions anchored to the bottom or the side of the window.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/sheets/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-sheet.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Secondary content. Sheets hold extra content and actions, not the main content of the app.
  • Match the window size. Use a bottom sheet in compact and medium windows and a side sheet in wider ones.
  • Standard or modal. A standard sheet sits beside the content so people can keep using it. A modal sheet blocks the page under a scrim until it is closed.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A bottom sheet has a container and an optional drag handle. A side sheet adds a headline, a close button and actions.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Bottom sheets

Link to “Bottom sheets” #

A bottom sheet rests at a partial height and expands when dragged or when its handle is activated. Without modal it is a standard sheet with no scrim. Set state="expanded" to open it at full height.

Without a drag handle

Link to “Without a drag handle” #

Add hide-drag-handle to remove the handle and dragging. Add skip-partially-expanded for a sheet that has no partial height.

Side sheets

Link to “Side sheets” #

A side sheet has a headline, a close button and an actions slot. Add divider to separate the actions, and detached to float the sheet with margins.

Back button

Link to “Back button” #

Set has-back-button on a side sheet to let people go back to an earlier region. The sheet fires back when it is pressed.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A modal sheet is a <dialog>: focus moves into it, stays inside, and returns to the opener on close. Escape and a click on the scrim close it.
  • Name a bottom sheet with label. A side sheet is named by its headline, or by label when it has none.
  • The drag handle is a button, so keyboard users can expand and collapse the sheet. Localize drag-handle-label, close-label and back-label.

App Bar

An app bar sits at the top of a screen and shows its title, navigation and actions, and can hide or compress as the page scrolls.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/app-bar/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-app-bar.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Keep it about the page. An app bar shows the title, navigation and a few actions that belong to the current page.
  • Limit the actions. Show one action, two if needed, and put many actions in a toolbar. Avoid an overflow menu when you can.
  • Pick a size. Use medium or large for a more expressive headline, and a small bar once content scrolls.
  • Let it respond to scrolling. It can hide or compress while people scroll.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

An app bar holds a leading navigation button, a title with an optional subtitle or image, and trailing actions.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Sizes

Link to “Sizes” #

Set size to md or lg for a taller bar. The default is sm.

Centered text

Link to “Centered text” #

Add centered to center the title and subtitle.

Search

Link to “Search” #

Set variant="search" and put a text input in the search slot.

Scroll behavior

Link to “Scroll behavior” #

Set scroll-behavior to hide to hide the bar while scrolling down, or to compress to turn a medium or large bar into a small one. Use scroll-target with the id of a scrolling element, or leave it out to follow the window.

Overflow actions

Link to “Overflow actions” #

On small windows only a few trailing actions show. The rest are listed in the overflowchange event, and the overflow slot holds a menu button that appears while actions are collapsed.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The title is the app bar's text, so make it match the page. Add context in an aria-label if the title alone is unclear.
  • Label every icon-only button with aria-label.
  • Tab moves through the buttons, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
  • A sticky or fixed app bar can cover focused content. Call setupScrollPadding() from scroll-padding.js so focused elements scroll clear of it.

Badge

A badge shows a small dot or a count to signal new or changed information.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/badge/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-badge.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use a dot for something new. A badge without content signals new or changed information.
  • Use a count for a number. A large badge shows a number, such as unread messages.
  • Keep counts short. Content is limited to four characters, including a +, so large numbers show as 999+.
  • Attach it to an icon. Anchor the badge to the top trailing corner of the icon it describes.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A badge is a single element. Without content it is a dot; with content it is a larger badge.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Count

Link to “Count” #

Set value to show a number. Counts above max (999 by default) show as max+.

Anchored

Link to “Anchored” #

Add anchored to place the badge on the top trailing corner of its positioned parent.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A dot badge is announced with its label, which defaults to "New notification". Set it to match your content.
  • Place the badge after the label of the destination it belongs to, so it is read in that order.

Card

A card contains content and actions about a single subject.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/card/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-card.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • One subject per card. A card shows related content and actions about a single topic, arranged so the hierarchy is clear.
  • Choose a color. Use elevated, filled or outlined to set how much the card stands out from its background.
  • Make it an entry point. An interactive card can lead to more detail or another page.
  • Lay out collections. Cards work in a grid, a vertical list or a carousel.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A card is a container with 16dp of inline padding around its content. The container slot replaces its background.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Set color to elevated, filled or outlined (default).

Interactive

Link to “Interactive” #

Add interactive to make the whole card a button. Add href to make it a link instead, and label it with aria-label.

Selectable

Link to “Selectable” #

Add selectable to an interactive card so activating it toggles selected. A selected card shows a check mark.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

A disabled card can't be activated.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • An interactive card has the button role, or the link role with href. Give it an accessible name with aria-label when its content isn't enough.
  • A card that isn't interactive is a plain container and needs no role. Its actions are focusable on their own.
  • Hide purely decorative images from assistive technology.
  • If a card can be dragged, offer a single-pointer alternative such as a menu with move and delete actions.
  • Tab moves to the next card or actionable element, and Enter or Space activates it.

Carousel

A carousel is a scrollable list of visual items that change size as they move through the layout.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/carousel/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-carousel.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Lead with visuals. Items emphasize an image and can carry a brief label that adapts to the item size.
  • Choose a layout. Use multi-browse for varied sizes, hero to feature an item, uncontained for items that run edge to edge, and full-screen for one item at a time.
  • Match scrolling to the layout. Snap scrolling suits multi-browse, hero and full-screen. Free scrolling suits uncontained.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A carousel holds md-gb-carousel-item elements. Each has a visual in its default slot and an optional label.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Hero

Link to “Hero” #

Set layout="hero" to feature a large item with small items beside it. Add alignment="center" to center it.

Uncontained

Link to “Uncontained” #

Set layout="uncontained" for items of one size that scroll freely. uncontained-multi-aspect allows items with different aspect ratios.

Linked items

Link to “Linked items” #

Give an item href to make it a link. Without it, the item is a button.

Scroll mode and orientation

Link to “Scroll mode and orientation” #

Set scroll-mode to snap or free, and orientation to horizontal or vertical. The full-screen layout scrolls vertically by default.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The carousel is a region with the role description "carousel". Name it with aria-label.
  • Each item's label is its accessible name, read with its position in the set.
  • Tab or the arrow keys move between items, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
  • Give images a text alternative, or hide decorative ones.

Checkbox

Checkboxes let people select one or more items from a set, or turn an option on or off.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/checkbox/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-checkbox.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Select from a set. Use checkboxes when people can pick any number of options from a list, or to turn one option on or off.
  • Label every checkbox. The label is the adjacent text, and it should say what checking the box does.
  • Use a parent for a group. A parent checkbox shows an indeterminate state when only some of its children are checked.
  • Don't apply density by default. Let people opt in to a denser layout.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A checkbox is one element. A <label> next to it, or around it, provides the text.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Checked and indeterminate

Link to “Checked and indeterminate” #

Add checked for a selected checkbox. Add indeterminate for a parent whose children are partly selected.

Error

Link to “Error” #

Add error to mark a checkbox as invalid. With required, it must be checked to submit a form.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

A disabled checkbox can't be changed.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) to -3 to shrink the checkbox. The touch target stays 48px.

Parent and children

Link to “Parent and children” #

Call linkParentCheckbox(parent, children) from checkbox-group.js. Checking the parent checks every child, and a partial selection makes the parent indeterminate.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The adjacent <label> text is the checkbox's accessible name. Use aria-label when there is no visible label or it needs more detail.
  • Space toggles the focused checkbox, and Tab moves between checkboxes.
  • A checkbox exposes its checked, unchecked or mixed state.

Chips

Chips help people enter information, make selections, filter content, or trigger actions.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/chip/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-chip.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Pick the type by purpose. Assist chips are smart actions, filter chips filter content, input chips are information a person entered, and suggestion chips offer dynamic replies or queries.
  • Show chips as a set. Unlike buttons, chips appear dynamically as a group, so always place them in a chip set.
  • Elevate only for protection. Use elevated chips when they sit on an image or a busy background.
  • Keep them compact. Reduce density when space is tight.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A chip set holds chips, and each chip holds its label and optional icons.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Assist chips

Link to “Assist chips” #

Assist chips are smart or automated actions, such as adding an event to a calendar. They are the default type, can link with href, and can be elevated.

Filter chips

Link to “Filter chips” #

Filter chips use tags or descriptive words to filter content and can replace toggle buttons or checkboxes. Set type="filter" and use selected for chosen ones.

Input chips

Link to “Input chips” #

Input chips are discrete pieces of information a person entered, such as contacts. Set type="input"; add removable for a remove button and editable to let people edit the text. Icons and avatars go in the icon slot.

Suggestion chips

Link to “Suggestion chips” #

Suggestion chips narrow a person's intent with dynamically generated suggestions, such as possible replies.

Chip set

Link to “Chip set” #

The chip set manages selection (selection="single" or "multiple") and arrow-key navigation, and wraps chips by default. With selection="single", add required so the selected chip can't be unselected, or single-line to scroll instead of wrap.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density on the chip set from 0 (default) to -3 to remove 4px of height per step.

Disabled and soft-disabled

Link to “Disabled and soft-disabled” #

A soft-disabled chip stays focusable so screen reader users can discover actions that are not available yet, such as Copy before text is selected.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A chip set is a grid of chips: label it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
  • Add an aria-label to chips whose text needs to be more descriptive.
  • The set is one tab stop; arrow keys, Home and End move between chips, and Backspace or Delete removes a removable chip.
  • Disabled chips leave the focus order; use soft-disabled where discoverability matters, per the ARIA guidance on disabled controls.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

Dialogs

Dialogs provide important prompts in a user flow.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/dialog/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-dialog.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use them sparingly. A dialog interrupts people to ask for a decision or to show critical information, so it blocks the rest of the app until it is dismissed.
  • Pick the right priority. For low or medium priority information, use a snackbar instead.
  • Choose basic or full-screen. Use a basic dialog by default. A full-screen dialog suits compact windows with a lot of content.
  • Order the actions. Put the dismissive action first and the confirming action last.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A dialog has an optional icon and headline, supporting content, and actions.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

With an icon

Link to “With an icon” #

Put an md-gb-icon in the icon slot to center the headline under a hero icon.

Full-screen

Link to “Full-screen” #

Set full-screen for a dialog that fills a compact window, with a close button and the confirming action in its header. Above compact sizes it falls back to a basic dialog; add always-full-screen to keep it.

Return value

Link to “Return value” #

A button's value becomes the dialog's returnValue when it closes the dialog through its form. Read it in the closed event.

Opening and closing

Link to “Opening and closing” #

Open and close a dialog with show() and close(), or by setting open. Both methods return a promise that resolves after the animation. Cancel the cancel event to keep the dialog open.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The headline names the dialog. Add aria-label to a dialog without a headline.
  • A basic dialog is an alert dialog (role="alertdialog") by default, as M3 asks for on the web. Set type="dialog" for a plain dialog.
  • Focus moves into the dialog and Tab cycles inside it. Escape closes it and focus returns to what opened it.
  • Label buttons and fields inside the dialog as you would elsewhere. In a full-screen dialog, set close-label to name the close button.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

alwaysFullScreen
Full-screen dialogs are for compact windows only (dialogs.md: use a basic dialog at medium and expanded). Turns off focus trapping, which keeps Tab and Shift+Tab cycling inside the dialog. Trapping is recommended for accessibility.		 no-focus-trap boolean false

Skips the opening and closing animations.		 quick boolean false

Divider

A divider is a thin line that groups content in lists and containers.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/divider/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-divider.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Group and create hierarchy. Dividers visually group components and can imply a parent and child relationship.
  • Full width for sections. Use full-width dividers to separate larger sections of unrelated content.
  • Inset for related items. Use inset dividers to separate related content within a section, such as items in a list.
  • Don't overuse. Spacing and type styles often separate content well enough on their own.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A divider is a single element.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Insets

Link to “Insets” #

Add inset to indent both ends by 16dp. Use inset-start or inset-end to indent only one end.

Vertical

Link to “Vertical” #

Add vertical for a divider between side-by-side content.

Class API

Link to “Class API” #

For plain HTML, the divider classes style a native <hr>. divider() is a Lit directive that adds them, and dividerClasses() returns them for other code. Pass {vertical: true} for a vertical divider.

Accessibility

  • A divider is decorative and not announced by assistive technology. It has no contrast minimum.
  • Add role="separator" to a divider that should be announced.

Lists

Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text and images, with optional selection, reordering, expanding and swipe actions.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/list/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-list.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Make items easy to scan. Keep labels short, order items in a logical way such as alphabetical or numerical, and show icons, text and actions in a consistent format.
  • Choose a style. A standard list is flat; a segmented list separates each item into its own container.
  • Match the item to its content. Add supporting text, an overline, an avatar or a leading icon to describe what an item is.
  • Add behavior when it helps. Lists can select, reorder, expand and reveal swipe actions.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A list holds list items. Each item has a label and slots around it.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Slots

Link to “Slots” #

An item's label is its default slot. Put an md-gb-icon in leading, a circular image or initial in avatar, a small line above the label in overline, and more detail in supporting-text.

Segmented

Link to “Segmented” #

Add segmented to show each item in its own container, separated by a small gap.

Non-interactive items

Link to “Non-interactive items” #

Add static to an item that only displays information, so it has no hover, focus or press states.

Selection

Link to “Selection” #

Add selectable to let people select several items with a long press, and by tapping while in selection mode. The list fires itemselectionchange, and selected items have checked. Add selection-primary when selecting is the main task, to always show the checkboxes.

Reordering

Link to “Reordering” #

Add reorderable to show a drag handle on every item. People can drag it, or tap it and use the move up and move down buttons. The list fires a cancelable reorder event.

Expandable items

Link to “Expandable items” #

Add expandable to an item and put a nested md-gb-list in its nested slot. Add expanded to start open.

Swipe actions

Link to “Swipe actions” #

Put buttons in the leading-actions and trailing-actions slots to reveal them when people swipe an item. A "more" button and the arrow keys offer the same actions without swiping.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density on the list from 0 (default) down to -3 to remove 4px of height per step. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A list has role="list", and role="listbox" when it is selectable. Items have role="listitem". Label a list with aria-label or aria-labelledby when its purpose isn't clear from the page.
  • Arrow keys move between items.
  • In a reorderable list, the drag handle and the move up and move down buttons have labels built from the item's text, and moves are announced to screen readers. Change them with drag-handle-label, move-up-label and move-down-label when you translate the page.
  • Give swipe action buttons an aria-label that names the item, such as "Share Fresh baked breads".
  • Selecting and reordering must not need a gesture only: the checkboxes, the move buttons and the "more" button are the single-pointer alternatives.

Menus

Menus show a temporary set of actions or choices, opened from a button, a text field or a context.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/menu/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-menu.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it for temporary actions. A menu shows a short set of actions on demand. To show actions on screen at all times, use a toolbar.
  • Open it from many places. A menu can open from a button, an icon button, a split button or a text field, or as a context menu.
  • Organize long menus. Use groups with labels and dividers to separate related choices.
  • Choose a color. The standard color suits most menus; vibrant makes the selected items stand out.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A menu holds items, groups and dividers. An item holds a label and optional slots, including a submenu.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Opening a menu

Link to “Opening a menu” #

A menu is a popover. Point an md-gb-button (or md-gb-icon-button, or a native button) at it with popovertarget, or call showPopover() from script. The menu positions itself next to the button and closes on Escape, when focus leaves, or when an item is chosen.

Icons and supporting text

Link to “Icons and supporting text” #

Fill the leading, supporting-text, trailing-text and trailing slots to add detail to an item.

Groups

Link to “Groups” #

Wrap related items in an md-gb-menu-group. Set label for a heading, and checkable to single or multiple to make the items selectable like radio buttons or checkboxes. Use checked on the selected items.

Grouped layout

Link to “Grouped layout” #

Set layout="grouped" to show each group on its own surface with a gap between them, instead of one surface with dividers.

Vibrant color

Link to “Vibrant color” #

Set color="vibrant" to use the tertiary color roles instead of the surface-based standard style.

Submenus

Link to “Submenus” #

Put an md-gb-menu in an item's submenu slot. It opens beside the item on click, Enter, Space or the Right arrow key (Left in right-to-left layouts).

Context menu

Link to “Context menu” #

Set context-for to the id of an element to open the menu on a secondary click, the context menu key or a long press.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) down to -3 to remove 4px of height per item for each step. Submenus inherit it. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The menu has role="menu", and items have role="menuitem", or menuitemradio and menuitemcheckbox in checkable groups.
  • On the button that opens the menu, Up and Down open it and focus the first item; Enter and Space open it natively.
  • In an open menu, Up and Down move between items (disabled items included), Home and End go to the first and last item, and typing a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it.
  • Escape and Tab close the menu and return focus to the button. Left (Right in right-to-left layouts) closes a submenu.
  • Give a menu that has no clear visible title an aria-label.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

color
The color style: standard (surface-based) or vibrant (tertiary).		 color MenuColor MENU_COLORS.standard
contextFor
The id of an element (in the same root) that opens this menu as a context menu on a secondary click, the context menu key or a long press (menus.md "Context menus ... usually open with a secondary click"; "Performs a specific action to trigger the menu, like right-click or press-and-hold").		 context-for string ''
density

The id of a text field (in the same root) the menu is attached to. As the person types in it, the menu opens (without taking focus) and shows only the items whose label contains the text, case-insensitively (menus.md "Filtering": "As someone types, the list of menu options filters to show relevant results"). The remaining items ease into their new position ("Menu items ease into their new position as the menu is filtered"), unless motion is reduced. Fires filter with the query.		 filter-for string ''

Radio

Radio buttons let people select one option from a set of options.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/radio/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-radio.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use radios for a single choice. Pick radio buttons, not switches, when only one option can be selected from a list; use checkboxes when several can.
  • Show every option. Radios expose all the choices, so use them for five or fewer; consider a menu when space is tight.
  • Always add a label. Each radio needs its own scannable label, and a person can select either the radio or its label.
  • Preselect one and stack them. List radios vertically with one option already selected, and avoid nesting them.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A radio is one element, paired with an adjacent label.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Group

Link to “Group” #

Radios with the same name form a group, and only one can be selected. Add checked to the one selected at the start, and value to identify the selection in a form.

Required

Link to “Required” #

Add required to any radio in the group to require a selection before the form submits.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

Add disabled to a radio that can't be selected right now.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) down to -3 to shrink the radio by 4px per step. The touch target stays 48px. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Place radios in a role="radiogroup" and label the group with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
  • Name each radio with a <label for> that points at its id. Use an aria-label only for a radio with no visible label.
  • Don't wrap a radio in its <label>; screen readers then can't announce the number of radios in the group.
  • Tab moves focus to the selected radio of a group, and the arrow keys move the selection between radios. Space selects the focused radio.
  • Once a radio is selected the group can't be cleared, so add a "None" option or a "Clear selection" control if people may opt out.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

Search

A search bar lets people enter a query and find matching results, with a search view that shows suggestions and results.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/search/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-search.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use it to navigate with queries. Search is the entry point for finding content in a product by typing.
  • Hint what to search. A bar can show hinted text such as "Search recipes", a leading icon and up to two trailing icons.
  • Suggest as people type. The view lists suggestions or results below the bar as the query changes.
  • Choose a style. The contained style is recommended; the divided style puts a divider between the header and the results.
  • Make it prominent. A search app bar gives search an emphasized, global entry point.

This component is new in M3 Expressive.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A search bar holds the leading and trailing elements; its default slot holds the suggestions or results shown in its search view.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Trailing elements

Link to “Trailing elements” #

Put up to two icon buttons in the trailing slot, or an avatar in the avatar slot. A leading icon button, such as a menu button, replaces the default search icon.

Docked

Link to “Docked” #

Add docked to open the view as a drop-down below the bar, for medium and larger windows. Without it, the view opens full-screen.

Divided

Link to “Divided” #

Add divided to use the baseline style, with a divider between the view's header and its results.

Search app bar

Link to “Search app bar” #

Put a search bar in the search slot of an app bar with variant="search". The app bar draws the container, so make the bar's container transparent.

Standalone search view

Link to “Standalone search view” #

Use md-gb-search-view on its own for a search that opens from an icon button. Set open from the button.

Searching

Link to “Searching” #

Set searching while you wait for results. The view shows a progress indicator and marks the results as busy.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The bar's input and the view's input are comboboxes, and the suggestions are the options of a listbox. Slotted results without a role get role="option".
  • Enter, the Down arrow or typing opens the view. The back button and Escape close it.
  • The input is named by label, which defaults to placeholder. Set label when the hint isn't a good name.
  • Give icon buttons in the slots an aria-label, such as "Voice search".
  • Change back-label, clear-label, results-label and searching-label when you translate the page. Announce changing results with suggestions-label.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

154 of 297 buildable spec units are tested, 13 are excluded with a written reason and 0 are uncovered (the target is 0). 60 of 79 token declarations match the spec (76%), and 19 have no spec token.

Select

Select menus let people choose one option from a list that opens on a temporary surface.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/select/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-select.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Fixed list of choices. Use a select to choose one value from a short, fixed list, like the native <select>. For a longer list that people can search, use the autocomplete.
  • Pick the variant by emphasis. Filled selects stand out more; outlined selects are lighter on dense forms.
  • Say what is wrong. Pair an error with text that explains how to fix it.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A select holds options and a field that shows the chosen one. Options can have icons and extra text.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Variants

Link to “Variants” #

Selects are filled by default. Set variant="outlined" for an outlined field.

Selected option

Link to “Selected option” #

Add selected to an option, or set value on the select, to choose one at the start.

Option content

Link to “Option content” #

Options take a leading icon, supporting-text, trailing-text and a trailing icon. Disabled options can't be chosen.

Leading icon

Link to “Leading icon” #

An icon in the leading-icon slot sits before the chosen text.

Error and supporting text

Link to “Error and supporting text” #

Use supporting-text for a hint. When error is set, error-text replaces it. Add required to mark the field as mandatory.

Autocomplete

Link to “Autocomplete” #

md-gb-autocomplete is a text field with the same options, filtered as people type. Set filter to change how options match.

In a form

Link to “In a form” #

A select takes part in a form through its name and value, and required is checked on submit.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The field is a combobox and the menu a listbox. The label names the field; add an aria-label when the label is elsewhere.
  • Enter, Space, or the arrow keys open the menu, the arrow keys move between options, and Escape closes it. Typing a few letters jumps to a matching option.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

Sliders

Sliders let people view and select a value, or a range of values, along a track.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/slider/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-slider.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Show the full range. A slider should present every value that can be chosen, with min and max set to match.
  • Apply the value right away. Use sliders for settings such as volume or brightness, where people see the effect as they drag.
  • Pick the variant by the value. A standard slider fills from the start, a centered slider fills from the middle, and a range slider selects two values.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A slider has a track, a handle, an optional value label and an optional icon.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Stops

Link to “Stops” #

Set step for a slider that snaps to values, and add ticks to show a stop at each one.

Centered

Link to “Centered” #

A centered slider starts its active track at the middle of the range, which suits values with a neutral point, such as balance.

Range

Link to “Range” #

Set range for two handles. Use value-start and value-end for the chosen values, and label-start and label-end to name the handles.

Icon and size

Link to “Icon and size” #

Put an icon in the icon slot to show it inside the track. Sizes run from xs (the default) to xl.

Vertical

Link to “Vertical” #

Set orientation="vertical" for a vertical slider. Range sliders can't be vertical.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

A disabled slider can't be changed and leaves the focus order.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Name every slider with an aria-label or a visible label. A range slider names each handle with label-start and label-end.
  • The handle is a slider that exposes its minimum, maximum and value. Set value-label (or value-label-start and value-label-end) when the number alone is unclear: the text is shown on the label and read out, such as "5 minutes".
  • Arrow keys change the value by one step, Page Up and Page Down by a larger amount, and Home and End jump to the ends.

Snackbar

Snackbars tell people about a process an app has performed or will perform, without interrupting them.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/snackbar/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-snackbar.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Low priority only. Use a snackbar for a message that needs no response. For an important one that blocks the task, use a dialog.
  • One at a time. Show a single snackbar, and queue consecutive messages.
  • At most one action. Give it a short action such as Undo. A snackbar with an action stays until it is used or dismissed.
  • Repeat the message nearby. A snackbar that disappears on its own is easy to miss, so also show the result inline, such as changing "Save" to "Saved".

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A snackbar has a message, an optional action and an optional close button.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Close button

Link to “Close button” #

Add has-close-button so people can dismiss the snackbar. Without an action it stays for timeout-ms (5 seconds by default); use -1 to keep it open.

Two lines

Link to “Two lines” #

Put longer text in the default slot for a two-line snackbar.

Consecutive snackbars

Link to “Consecutive snackbars” #

md-gb-snackbar-host shows messages one after another. Call showSnackbar(); it resolves with action-performed or dismissed. Pass replace: true to swap out a message that is out of date.

Anchor

Link to “Anchor” #

Set anchor to the id of an element, such as a FAB, so the snackbar appears above it.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The message is announced politely in a live region, so focus stays where it is.
  • Auto-dismissing snackbars are hard to read for people with low vision or who need more time. Give the same information inline, or add an action so the snackbar stays until it is used.
  • Give a snackbar that has a close button a localized close-label.
  • Escape closes the snackbar, and a slotted action is a normal button in the tab order.

Link to “Slots” #
Slot Description
default Default slot for rich content (rendered after label-text). If both label-text and slotted content are provided, both render.
action Slot for a custom action button; replaces the built-in action rendered from action-label. Prefer the action-label attribute, which renders a text button matching the spec. A slotted plain <button> is styled by the snackbar, with hover, focus and pressed states. A slotted text <md-gb-button> gets the --action-label-text* colors and typography, but keeps its own 16px padding and pressed shape, because its component tokens can't be set from outside its shadow root.

Switch

Switches toggle the state of an item on or off.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/switch/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-switch.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Use for settings. Switches are the best way to let people adjust a setting. Use a switch, not a radio button, when each item in a list is controlled on its own.
  • Visible at a glance. Make the on or off state clear, and let the change take effect right away.
  • Label with text. Put the label next to the switch in a <label>. Its text color stays the same, even when the switch changes.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A switch has a track, a handle and optional icons shown in the handle.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Selected

Link to “Selected” #

Add selected to start with the switch on.

Icons

Link to “Icons” #

Icons in the on-icon and off-icon slots appear in the handle. Fill only on-icon to show an icon just when the switch is on.

Disabled

Link to “Disabled” #

A disabled switch can't be changed.

In a form

Link to “In a form” #

A switch submits its value (on by default) under its name when it is selected, and required means it must be on.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A switch has the switch role. It takes its name from an adjacent <label>, or from an explicit aria-label, which wins over the label.
  • Add an aria-label to a switch with no visible label.
  • Space toggles the switch.

Tabs

Tabs organize groups of related content that are at the same level of hierarchy.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/tabs/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-tabs.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Same level of hierarchy. Tabs switch between views of related content that are peers. Don't use them for steps in a flow.
  • Primary or secondary. Primary tabs sit at the top of the content under a top app bar and show the main destinations. Secondary tabs split a content area further. Use one type in a bar.
  • Short labels. Keep labels to a word or two. Use icons only when they are simple and recognizable.
  • Avoid dense tabs by default. Lowering the density shrinks the targets below 48px, so let people opt in.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A tab list holds tabs, and each tab has an optional icon, a label and an optional badge. Tab panels hold the content.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Primary and secondary

Link to “Primary and secondary” #

Tabs are primary by default. Set variant="secondary" for secondary tabs, which put the icon beside the label.

Icons

Link to “Icons” #

Put an icon before the label, or leave out the label for icon-only tabs. Icon-only tabs need an aria-label.

Badges

Link to “Badges” #

A tab can show a badge in the badge slot for counts or status.

Tab panels

Link to “Tab panels” #

Link each tab to its panel with tabpanel, the id of a panel such as md-aria-tabpanel. Only the selected panel is shown.

Swipeable panels

Link to “Swipeable panels” #

md-gb-tab-panels holds the panels next to the tabs and lets people swipe between them. It pairs with the previous tab list, or with for, the id of one. Set gestures-disabled to turn swiping off.

Scrollable

Link to “Scrollable” #

Fixed tabs share the width equally. Set scrollable to size each tab to its label and scroll the bar when they overflow.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) to -3 to remove 4px of height per step.

Selection events

Link to “Selection events” #

The tab list fires change when a person picks a tab. Read the new tab from selectedTabIndex.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • Tabs use the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles. Label the tab list with aria-label or aria-labelledby, and give icon-only tabs an aria-label.
  • The list is one tab stop. The arrow keys move between tabs, and Space or Enter selects the focused one.
  • Each tab controls a panel, and each panel is labelled by its tab. Linking them with tabpanel or md-gb-tab-panels does this for you.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

87 of 206 buildable spec units are tested, 12 are excluded with a written reason and 0 are uncovered (the target is 0). 41 of 56 token declarations match the spec (73%), and 15 have no spec token.

Text field

Text fields let people enter and edit text.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/text-field/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-text-field.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Filled or outlined. Filled fields have more visual weight and suit most forms. Outlined fields are lighter and work where many fields sit together. Don't mix them in one form.
  • Label every field. The label floats above the text once the field has a value or focus. Use a placeholder only as an example of the input, never in place of the label.
  • Help before and after. Use supporting text for hints, and explain what went wrong in an error.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A text field has a label, the input, optional icons and prefix or suffix text, and supporting text.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Variants

Link to “Variants” #

Text fields are filled by default. Set variant="outlined" for an outlined field. Add placeholder for an example of the input.

Input types

Link to “Input types” #

type changes the keyboard and the built-in validation. It can be text (default), email, number, password, search, tel, url or textarea.

Textarea

Link to “Textarea” #

type="textarea" makes a multi-line field. Set rows for its height.

Icons

Link to “Icons” #

Icons in the leading-icon and trailing-icon slots sit before and after the input. A trailing icon button needs an aria-label.

Prefix and suffix

Link to “Prefix and suffix” #

prefix-text and suffix-text show fixed text around the input, such as a currency or a domain.

Supporting text and counter

Link to “Supporting text and counter” #

supporting-text shows a hint below the field. A maxlength adds a character counter.

Error and validation

Link to “Error and validation” #

Set error and error-text to show an error yourself. A field also validates with the browser's constraint attributes (required, pattern, minlength, min, max) when its form is submitted or reportValidity() is called, and shows the message in its supporting text.

Required

Link to “Required” #

required adds an asterisk to the label and makes an empty field invalid. Add no-asterisk to hide it.

Disabled and read-only

Link to “Disabled and read-only” #

A disabled field can't be focused. A readonly field can be focused and selected but not edited.

In a form

Link to “In a form” #

Fields take part in a form through their name and value, and the form checks them on submit.

Density

Link to “Density” #

Set density from 0 (default) to -3 to remove 4px of height per step.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • The field's label names the input. For a field with an external label, add an aria-label.
  • Supporting and error text are linked to the input, so screen readers read them with it. An invalid field is marked with aria-invalid.
  • Icon buttons in a slot need their own aria-label.

Toolbar

A toolbar holds actions that relate to the content on the screen, docked to an edge or floating above it.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/toolbar/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-toolbar.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Actions for the page. A toolbar offers actions related to the current page and can show more of them in larger windows.
  • Docked or floating. A docked toolbar spans the window and suits global actions that stay the same across pages. A floating toolbar hovers over the content and suits actions for that content.
  • Vibrant for emphasis. Use the vibrant color for more emphasis.
  • Not with a navigation bar. Don't show a toolbar at the same time as a navigation bar.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A toolbar holds actions, such as buttons and icon buttons. A floating toolbar can have a FAB.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Colors

Link to “Colors” #

Toolbars are standard by default. Set color="vibrant" for a more prominent toolbar.

Docked

Link to “Docked” #

Add docked to stretch the toolbar across the full width of its container.

Buttons with labels

Link to “Buttons with labels” #

Toolbars can hold buttons with labels as well as icon buttons. Use toggle buttons to show a selected state.

Orientation

Link to “Orientation” #

Set orientation="vertical" to stack the actions in a column.

With a FAB

Link to “With a FAB” #

A floating toolbar can sit beside a FAB in the fab slot. Set fab-position="start" to move it to the leading side, or expanded="false" to collapse the toolbar to just the FAB.

Overflow

Link to “Overflow” #

Add overflow-menu to move trailing actions that don't fit into a "More actions" menu.

Hide on scroll

Link to “Hide on scroll” #

Set scroll-behavior="hide" to move a docked or floating toolbar off screen when the page scrolls down and bring it back when it scrolls up. scroll-target names the element that scrolls; it defaults to the window.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A toolbar has the toolbar role. Label it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
  • Every action stays in the Tab order, and the arrow keys also move between them (up and down in a vertical toolbar).
  • Icon-only actions need an aria-label.
  • A collapsed toolbar makes its hidden actions inert.

Tooltip

Tooltips add context to a button or other element, as a short plain label or a richer panel with a subhead and actions.

Online: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/tooltip/

Install with shadcn/ui: npx shadcn@latest add https://material-web.dev/3.0/r/md-tooltip.json (setup)

Usage guidelines

Link to “Usage guidelines” #
  • Plain to label. Use a plain tooltip to name an element with no text, such as an icon-only button. Don't add one when the element already has a visible label.
  • Rich for details. Use a rich tooltip for longer text, such as a definition or an explanation of a new feature, with an optional subhead and up to two text buttons.
  • Nothing critical. Tooltips are easy to miss, so never hide information people must see. Use a dialog for that.

Anatomy

Link to “Anatomy” #

A tooltip points at an anchor element by its id. A rich tooltip can add a subhead and actions.

Examples

Link to “Examples” #

Placement

Link to “Placement” #

A plain tooltip opens above its anchor and a rich one below it. Set placement to above, below, start or end; it flips when there isn't room. Add caret to point at the anchor.

Rich

Link to “Rich” #

Set variant="rich" and a subhead. Text buttons go in the action slot.

Persistent

Link to “Persistent” #

A persistent rich tooltip opens when the anchor is clicked and stays open until someone interacts with something else, so people can reach its actions.

Delays

Link to “Delays” #

A tooltip opens right away and closes 1.5 seconds after the pointer leaves. Set show-delay and hide-delay in milliseconds, or add quick to skip the motion.

Accessibility

Link to “Accessibility” #
  • A plain tooltip is a tooltip that describes its anchor, and it opens on hover and on keyboard focus. Keep the anchor's own accessible name, such as an aria-label on an icon button.
  • A rich tooltip with actions is a dialog, so its buttons can be reached with the keyboard.
  • Escape closes an open tooltip.
  • Don't put information in a tooltip that people can't find another way, since touch users can't hover.

Compatibility

Link to “Compatibility” #

API reference

Link to “API reference” #

<md-gb-tooltip>

Link to “<md-gb-tooltip>” #

A Material Design plain or rich tooltip.

Properties

Link to “Properties” #
Property Attribute Type Default
align
How the tooltip lines up with its anchor along the placement side: center (plain default) or start (rich default). A rich tooltip can be centered below its anchor on desktop.		 align "" "start"
caret
Whether to draw a caret pointing at the anchor.		 caret boolean false
hideDelay
Delay before hiding after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds.		 hide-delay number TOOLTIP_HIDE_DELAY_MS
htmlFor
The id of the anchor element, in the same root as the tooltip.		 for string ''
noBoundary
Plain only: the anchor has no visual boundary, such as a text baseline, so the tooltip sits 8dp from it instead of 4dp.		 no-boundary boolean false
open
Whether the tooltip is open.		 open boolean
persistent
Rich only: opens when the anchor is clicked instead of on hover / focus, and stays open until the user interacts with another element.		 persistent boolean false
placement
Preferred side of the anchor. Defaults to above for plain tooltips and below for rich ones. Flips when there isn't room.		 placement "" TooltipPlacement
quick
Skips the open / close animation.		 quick boolean false
showDelay
Hover delay before showing, in milliseconds.		 show-delay number TOOLTIP_SHOW_DELAY_MS
subhead
Rich only: subhead text. Replaced by content in the subhead slot.		 subhead string ''
variant
Plain or rich.		 variant TooltipVariant TOOLTIP_VARIANTS.plain

Slots

Link to “Slots” #
Slot Description
default The supporting text.
action Rich tooltip text buttons (up to two), e.g. <md-gb-button color="text">.
subhead Rich tooltip subhead; replaces the subhead attribute.

Events

Link to “Events” #
Event Description
close
CustomEvent<{reason: string}>		 Fired before the tooltip closes. Cancelable.
closed
CustomEvent<{reason: string}>		 Fired after the tooltip closes.
open
Event		 Fired before the tooltip opens. Cancelable.
opened
Event		 Fired after the tooltip opens.

Methods

Link to “Methods” #
Method Description
hide
() => void		 Closes the tooltip.
reposition
() => void		 Recomputes the tooltip's position next to its anchor.
show
() => void		 Opens the tooltip, closing any other open tooltip.
